The president of the Swiss Football Association, Peter Knabel, said: “Granit Xhaka approached us about the situation last [Sunday] night and told us he would admit it publicly and take responsibility. We welcome Granit taking this step and facing the consequences. We jointly concluded that it is in the team’s interests to complete the entire camp without him. Our priority now is to calm the situation.”

Although the Swiss FA possess the power to hit Xhaka with a suspension from football – something they could ask Fifa to apply worldwide – that scenario is regarded as highly unlikely.

Sports.title: Paper trail of protests: José Mourinho plays the hits in Madrid derby defeat | Sid Lowe
Sports.content:
There were many questions to emerge from the Madrid derby, which Atlético won 2-1 in front of 70,514 very, very noisy people at the Metropolitano on Sunday afternoon, even if not the one José Mourinho was asking. Like: what year is this? Or: what was Dean Huijsen thinking? Why always Arda? And whatever happened to Vinícius Júnior? How come Koke is still the best? And how long before Giuliano Simeone actually bursts, his atlético insides exploding across the pitch? Above all though, you were left wondering: where did Real Madrid’s manager get a printer from? And how did he get the bloody thing to work?

You could still hear the singing outside when Mourinho turned up in the press room, laid down his glasses and sat. In his hand was a piece of paper. Thirteen years after his last derby, on the Santiago Bernabéu night when Madrid lost the Copa del Rey final and a 13-year unbeaten run against their neighbours, Diego Simeone had defeated him again. The stage was new – this stadium didn’t exist then – but his adversary was somehow still the same man, still dressed in black, and the scene was a bit like old times, a classic. Mourinho unfolded the paper and held it up. “We can save ourselves the bother of the press conference,” he said, “because the story is right here.”

Printed on the back side of an Atlético info sheet were two screen grabs from the first half, one on top of the other. Someone had been sent to run off a copy, some footballing Natalie Harp or the manager himself coming back with a couple of gory, freeze-framed, full-colour closeups of tackles. The first showed Cuti Romero’s studs catching Jude Bellingham’s knee; the second showed Kang-in Lee on Fede Valverde’s ankle. Both should have been red, Mourinho insisted, and he was probably right, but neither was. It should have been nine against 11, he said; instead, it was 11 against 10 because early in the second half Huijsen dragged Giuliano Simeone down for the penalty that gave Atlético the lead and got him sent off. And that, Mourinho said, was that. End of story.

View image in fullscreen Real Madrid’s Dean Huijsen was sent off after conceding a penalty to Atlético’s Giuliano Simeone during the derby. Photograph: Juan Carlos Lucas/Zuma Press Wire/Shutterstock

At which point he could have got up and gone, saved everyone the bother of the press conference like he promised, but no one wants that, least of all his president, and that’s the bit he does best so he carried on. Five questions he faced. Four of them were about the referee; so was the answer to the one that was not about the referee. And when he had finished, leaving the paper there for Diego Simeone to have a look at, most agreed: now Mourinho is back, and he’s playing the greatest hits, a hint of the nostalgia that had brought him “home” in the first place, a hint of the conspiratorial mindset too, echoes of him reading out 13 “errors” made by the referee Clos Gómez 16 years earlier.

The “poor ref” – just 41, not an international, and named in advance rather than 24 hours before kick-off – couldn’t handle the pressure, which was “like the 1980s”, Mourinho claimed. The coach, who had already revived his famous “por qué” (why?) line after they lost at Betis, also ran through a list of decisions made by the referee in the VAR room, Daniel Trujillo Suárez – a man supposedly with history – which “make you laugh”. There was talk of “strange things” happening. He insisted he didn’t want to think ill of officials, didn’t want to say the league has been “set up” for others to win, didn’t want to think that these were anything other than honest mistakes – of course not. He congratulated the referees’ committee and vowed to fight for the title despite being six points behind already – if they let us. “I thought I would come back to find a different league to the one I left, but [at Madrid] they told me not and explained why not,” he said.

What Mourinho didn’t say was anything really about the actual football, which might be because there wasn’t much football. The cards might have conditioned the game – of course they might – and he was entitled to insist on the reds, although you could debate Romero’s. But it was hard to avoid the feeling that Mourinho purposely missed a deeper point and revealed a deeper reality, that there could be no escaping the reality he sought to escape: that Madrid are just not very good. That too many questions were avoided and another could be asked: is that it? There was little evidence to back his brief claim that they played well in the first half and were set up to win it in the second – how? – and even if true, it pointed to something limited: wait, counter and it will come.

With the players Madrid have, often it will, but Atlético were aware of that, planned for it; they were aware too of where the damage could be done, overloading Madrid’s left. Simeone’s side took more than twice as many shots and had two-thirds of the possession. They had done so cautiously, it is true, but they, not Madrid, had exercised control. Mourinho’s team had offered little before the potential reds, their first shot on target coming on 39 minutes and from 25 yards, and even less after the actual red, Atlético’s half unoccupied for most of the period except by a pigeon. With Guler withdrawn, their reaction didn’t exist. It’s not easy with 10 men, but there was barely a spark. Even the goal they did get in the 89th minute was an isolated moment and, for all the nerves at the Metropolitano, was followed by more chances for Atlético.

Thank you for your feedback.

None of which would matter so much as a one-off, but these flaws were familiar. Madrid needed last-minute Carlos Espí goals to beat Espanyol and Elche and they’re still six points off the top already. It’s not even close to definitive just seven weeks in and Madrid’s rebuilding process has only just begun, but basic issues they have faced for the last two years remain unaddressed; Fabio Capello’s implausible 2006-07 league title win is the only time Barcelona have ever had a lead that big at the top of the table and lost it. Hansi Flick’s team are flying; and right now you wouldn’t trust Madrid to take advantage even if they did slip up. Claude Makélélé summed them up as: “Nothing, nothing, nothing.” Which leaves only this: a print-out and paranoia, a campaign. Some things don’t change. Some people don’t change much, either.

View image in fullscreen Jonathan David (right) score the winner in a Madrid derby which Atlético dominated. Photograph: Alberto Gardin/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

Some, though, do. The last time these two coaches met in a derby, Simeone’s son Giuliano was told he was too little to go to the final so he hung scarves around the living room and watched it from home with his brothers instead. It was late, it was a school night, and he was only 10. He is 23 now and these days he plays for them, a bundle of intensity going at it the way a fan would, and on the day these two “colleagues of war” – as Mourinho called them – met again 13 years later he decided the derby, forcing the penalty for the first and setting up the second. There is some footage somewhere of Giuliano as a ballboy racing up the touchline and leaping into his father’s arms, celebrating wildly when Atlético scored against Madrid. A decade on, another derby day, and it happened again, only this time it was his dad sprinting up the line towards him.

Talking points

“We give him the ball, he scores the goals,” Fermín López said. Over and over and over again. Raphinha, who is filling in at centre forward, has now scored 12 league goals in just seven games, plus two more in the Champions League. He is five ahead of anyone else already. On Saturday night he scored an outrageously good hat-trick, the movement every inch the No 9, the touch and finishing at ridiculous speed all his, as Barcelona beat Sevilla 3-1. Sevilla went a goal up and were as good as anyone against Flick’s side so far this season but in the end just couldn’t live with them, coach Luis García calling them “stratospheric”. That’s seven wins from seven (eight from eight in all competitions), and 31 goals already, the captain leading the way. And not just with the goals, but with everything, taking everyone on a wild intense ride with him. Raphinha says that Lamine Yamal should win the Ballon d’Or but right now there’s no one quite like him anywhere. That said, Lamine Yamal was absurd at the Pizjuan.

At the end of their 0-0 draw with Athletic, Alavés goalkeeper Antonio Sivera walked off saying: “At last, at last!” His record was, he said, “ridiculous” but now at last he had done it. A European champion at U21 level, he is 30 now, and he had just saved the first penalty of his entire career.

“When I played football as a kid in Croatia, everyone wants to play in one of Europe’s top five leagues and on my list Spain was bottom, but in the end it seems like Osasuna and La Liga is my place: God’s path is different to mine,” said Ante Budimir on Saturday, after a lovely chest-and-volley goal took him to 100 in Spain.

Speaking of which, what a way to celebrate the 100th birthday of your home.

Sports.title: Ghosts of 2023 quelled after Dortmund return to the Bundesliga summit | Andy Brassell
Sports.content:
Borussia Dortmund would probably rather not think about the last time that they topped the Bundesliga. It was in May 2023, just before all their dreams imploded, with black and yellow Deutscher Meister t-shirts – ‘German champions’ – for sale on the approach to Signal Iduna Park and cold beers at the ready. Now, that is no longer the most recent time Dortmund have led the pack.

It’s four games, four wins to start this season and the Niko Kovac workout plan is hitting the spot. Saturday night’s single-goal win at Stuttgart was a game that had the gravitas of a true Topspiel, if not quite the entertainment value of one. Kovac’s fingerprints were all over it. The conversation of whether his view of the game fits with BVB’s swashbuckling image will no doubt continue, but this was a case in point to show just how good Kovac has been for the club, and for the team.

Dortmund had taken four points from the two games against Sebastian Hoeness and his Stuttgart team last season – and just as Kovac will not be oblivious to criticism of his side’s style, nor is Hoeness to whispers about his impressive team’s waning record against direct rivals – but were hardly overwhelmingly impressive either. It had been a huge improvement on the 2024-25 encounters with Stuttgart, in which BVB had been well beaten, twice, once under the short reign of Nuri Sahin and once in Kovac’s first game in charge, at which point he must have realised the mountainous task ahead of him.

Here, in September 2026, was the clearest of markers of how far Dortmund have come under the former Croatia midfielder and how deeply his ideas have taken root. To see a Dortmund patient, poised and defensively competent enough to grind this game out is still a novelty, and they didn’t have a shot on target until Maximilian Beier prodded in the winner from an inviting ball in by substitute Jobe Bellingham. That Dortmund dealt with everything the home side had in response, with street smarts and limited fuss, was laudable. They made a very accomplished attacking forced look ordinary. “In a top match,” Stuttgart’s Hoeness later reflected, “decent and okay aren’t enough.”

That Bellingham and Beier combined for the goal was noteworthy too; the former frequently rubbished for not being the equal of his generationally-talented elder brother and the latter another player who is simply underrated, both were brought in for big money and accordingly viewed with little patience. Their adaptability was striking, with Bellingham impacting off the bench and Beier thriving in a more advanced role. They are both Kovac’s type: young, willing, athletic and adaptable.

View image in fullscreen Niko Kovac has been in charge of Borussia Dortmund since January 2025. Photograph: Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

Should we call Dortmund contenders? That is, perhaps, a bit strong. But there is talk is about reducing the 16-point gap to Bayern that remained at the end of last season, and there were signs here that they may, at least, be capable of that. “It’s about annoying Bayern a bit”, is how Dortmund managing director Lars Ricken framed it, following the win at Stuttgart.

Dortmund were never going to return to relevance and consistency by trying to relive the Jürgen Klopp years, or by trying to ape Bayern (and yes, both of those approaches have been attempted). To get into the position where they can face the hurt (and potential rewards) of 2023 all over again will take a while, and doesn’t just depend on them – it will take Bayern falling down a rung or two. They are at least climbing the right ladder though, slowly, steadily, and diligently.

Thank you for your feedback.

Talking points

It was only a matter of time and it was probably always going to happen against an ailing Union Berlin, who are enduring a horrible start to the season, but Harry Kane reached 100 Bundesliga goals on Friday night in his 98th game, so much faster than anyone in the league’s history. His double was almost a footnote on a night as Michael Olise scored a dazzling hat-trick, with Jamal Musiala and Ismaël Saibari also netting their first league goals of the season in a 7-0 shellacking. It was a good start to the club’s traditional celebration of Oktoberfest weekend.

Bayern later mourned Peter Hermann, Jupp Heynckes’ popular assistant in the 2013 treble-winning season, who passed away on Saturday at the age of 73. Hermann was also emotionally commemorated at Leverkusen before kick-off on Sunday, having played in their 1979 promotion-winning team and having later served as assistant to Klaus Toppmöller at the helm of the celebrated 2002 Champions League finalists. Die Werkself paid fitting tribute on the field too as they beat RB Leipzig 2-0. The margins were fine, with Christopher Nkunku having an opener ruled out for the visitors before Patrik Schick put the home side ahead from a Miguel Gutiérrez cross. Gutiérrez, Álex Grimaldo’s nominal replacement, scored the second himself. Carles Martínez praised his team for “good balance between keeping the ball and playing forward”, while his opposite number Martín Demichelis has plenty to think about after a fourth straight away defeat.

View image in fullscreen Bayer Leverkusen players and fans hold a minute of silence for Peter Hermann. Photograph: Martin Meissner/AP

Never before had a team scored three times in successive Bundesliga home games and lost both of them but Borussia Mönchengladbach are managing to find a ledge beneath the edge. Gladbach made a bright start against Mainz (who are under interim coach Jan-Moritz Lichte) – with Florian Neuhaus scoring the opener on his return to the line-up, his first since May 2024 – but ended in defeat again, leaving them bottom, without a point. Alexander Blessin, a former St Pauli coach famed for his defensive work, is expected to arrive in an attempt to plug the leaks.

Hamburg had gone into matchday four pointless and goalless but managed to squeeze past a Köln side who dominated them, with Yussuf Poulsen’s second goal for the club since arriving in summer 2025 proving decisive. It was an endorsement of their faith in head coach Merlin Polzin, who signed a contract extension this week despite that bad start and successive 5-0 defeats.

There are comebacks and there are comebacks, and several coincided on the Weser as Werder Bremen continued their surprisingly good start to the season. They trailed 2-0 to Augsburg but were level after a Niclas Füllkrug netbuster but even better was around the corner, with Mitchell Weiser rattling in a perfect left-foot winner, deep into stoppage time, in his first home appearance after 16 months out with injury. It brought the former Bayern man to tears and his coach Daniel Thoune described it as “a goosebump moment”.

All three promoted teams now have a win after Paderborn’s shock victory over Hoffenheim in Sunday’s late game, with veteran substitute Steffen Tigges sealing it with a header for his first top-flight goal since 2024. It was a third loss in four for Hoffenheim, who also suffered an embarrassing Europa League reverse at OFI Crete on Thursday.

Sports.title: Pierre Sage took Lens to new heights. His replacement left after six games
Sports.content:
It was under cover of darkness that Yannick Cahuzac took his place in the Lens dugout at the Stade Louis II on Friday night. The lights dimmed as the players made their entrance and Cahuzac, who had been named interim manager just three days earlier, sat alone, leaning forward on a seat that Dino Toppmöller would have occupied if not for a dramatic turn of events last week.

Cahuzac’s appointment, much like his entrance in Monaco, had a stealthy quality, as if he had always been there and the switching of the lights was mere confirmation of his presence. Cahuzac left Lorient, where he had been Olivier Pantaloni’s assistant, at the end of last season to return to Lens, where he had finished his playing career before working as Franck Haise’s assistant in the 2022–23 campaign.

He was spoken about as a future No 1, but that was not the role he took in the summer. Cahuzac is still an apprentice who has not yet obtained his coaching qualifications so he returned to the club as an assistant to Toppmöller. The German had the unenviable task of succeeding Pierre Sage, who hastily departed to Crystal Palace after guiding Lens to a maiden Coupe de France triumph and a second-place finish in Ligue 1 last season.

Lens were not expected to soar as high this season. Speaking in the summer, the club’s sporting director, Jean-Louis Leca, said they were “not a Champions League club” and that an eighth-place finish in Ligue 1 would represent success. Toppmöller’s first game in charge brought silverware as Lens beat PSG in the Trophée des Champions; his first Ligue 1 game was a resounding 5-2 win over Auxerre; and his side took all three points away to Slavia Prague in their first Champions League game – not a bad start after a summer of upheaval and the departure of several important players.

Results have dipped in recent weeks but expectations were being met. Hence the shock last week when it was announced that the German had left the club by mutual consent. Having taken charge of just six games, Toppmöller is Lens’s shortest-serving manager since the second world war. His exit says more about the club than it does the man. Explaining the parting of ways, the chief executive, Benjamin Parrot, revealed a divide, not necessarily between Toppmöller and his squad, but rather within the staff itself.

“Even before the Trophée des Champions, we felt, within the staff, that there was a French group and then a more international group,” said Parrot. Toppmöller brought two assistants with him. Lens tried to sack one of them, Nelson Morgado, but Toppmöller stayed loyal to his assistant and refused to accept his dismissal. He left and Cahuzac stepped up in his place.

View image in fullscreen Paris Brunner and Denis Zakaria embrace after Monaco take the lead in their win against Lens. Photograph: Alunno Nicolas/Abaca/Shutterstock

Cahuzac was touted as Toppmöller’s successor before he had even settled at the club. That can’t be a healthy environment for any new manager. Perhaps the writing was always on the wall for Toppmöller, especially given that Leca – Cahuzac’s close friend and former teammate at Bastia – is the club’s sporting director. Leca knows how it looks. “Yes, he is my friend, but inside these walls he isn’t my friend. Inside these walls, I am his line manager,” said Leca.

To suggest that Cahuzac’s appointment is pure nepotism is unfair. Lorient were one of the most tactically interesting teams in Ligue 1 last season and while Pantaloni – who was nominated for the manager-of-the-season award – earned most of the plaudits, Cahuzac played a key role too. He also knows the club, having played for them for three seasons and worked under Haise as an assistant.

His first game in charge, against Monaco, did not begin well. The hosts were 1-0 up at half-time but they had the ball in the Lens net on three occasions, denied by the assistant referee’s flag. Cahuzac changed tactics at the interval, which helped, and Matthieu Udol headed in a deserved equaliser. Franjo Ivanovic and Thorgan Hazard had chances as Lens pushed for a winner. In the end, it was a Lens player who scored but, unfortunately for Jonathan Gradit, it was into his own net.

So, Cahuzac’s tenure begins with a valiant 2-1 defeat. The 41-year-old was a pitbull of a player but he was almost inert in his dugout. He stood like a statue, with his hand on his chin in a pensive pose that exuded a studious serenity. After the turbulent week Lens have had, the club need a sense of calm.

Talking points

On the topic of messy break-ups, there was an unhappy reunion between Liam Rosenior and Strasbourg on Saturday. The pair had not met since Rosenior was hurried out the door to join sister club Chelsea in January. There is no love lost. The Englishman led Paris FC to a 2-1 win, continuing his unbeaten run since returning to Ligue 1 this summer. He celebrated the win in front of the travelling Strasbourg fans, a response, Rosenior said, to insulting chants about his family from the away end. An unsavoury confrontation between both sets of players and staff ensued. Rosenior said the chants had gone “too far” and that “celebrating like that was clearly a message”. His players also sent a message, confirming that they are in the mix for Champions League qualification.

View image in fullscreen Liam Rosenior celebrated Paris FC’s win in front of the travelling Strasbourg fans. Photograph: Matthieu Mirville/Zuma Press Wire/Shutterstock

PSG beat Marseille 2-1 in a Classique that encapsulated the clubs’ seasons so far; both are struggling. For PSG, the points are at least now flowing. Ferran Torres continues to prove a fine signing. He came off the bench to score the opening goal. Marquinhos redeemed himself for his own goal in this fixture last season, which gave Marseille their first win over PSG at the Vélodrome in Ligue 1 in 14 years. That feels like a long time ago now. The concerns for Marseille only deepen. There were bright moments, notably Angel Gomes’s equaliser, but Bruno Génésio’s side have now lost four of their first five league matches. “A Ligue 2 project?” read a banner from the home fans. They go into the international break in the relegation zone.

Despite the game being briefly suspended after the home fans unfurled an insulting banner that targeted their fierce rivals Saint-Étienne, Lyon made a statement with a 4-0 win over Rennes. They rotated in their midweek Europa League win over Anderlecht, a clear but disappointing sign of where their priorities lie. It paid off, however. Rennes fielded a stronger side against Sturm Graz but did not take the three points, and their striker Esteban Lepaul was consequently not involved from the start against Lyon. A full-strength Lyon made short work of Franck Haise’s side, who may struggle to balance their European and league commitments. Rennes did not lay a glove on Lyon, whose own fans posed the greatest threat.

This is an article by Get French Football News

Sports.title: Israel's FA accuse Ireland manager of 'ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity' after he commented 'we're playing against genocide' before match which critics want cancelled over Gaza
Sports.content:
Israel's FA accuse Ireland manager of 'ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity' after he commented 'we're playing against genocide' before match which critics want cancelled over Gaza

The Israeli FA angrily took to social media on Monday to hit back at Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson's comments when he used the word 'genocide' in previewing the upcoming fixtures.

The Icelandic boss used forceful language in defending his team as they prepare to take the field against a side that the Football Association of Ireland wanted to have suspended from competitions.

'And I've said before, we're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide,' he said at the weekend. 'So, we're playing against Israel. We're not playing with Israel.'

As reports circulated that the Israelis were considering a complaint to UEFA, the Israeli FA posted on X on Monday night: 'We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way,' the post on X stated.

'Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by the Republic of Ireland team coach.

'We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them.'

Israel's FA have accused Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson of 'ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity' after his 'genocide' comments

The Israeli FA are now set to report Hallgrimsson to UEFA.

The Ireland chief oversaw training at Abbotstown as he fine-tunes preparations for Thursday's meeting with Kosovo in Pristina, but it's the meeting with Israel in Debrecen in Hungary on Sunday, and in Backa Topola in Serbia a week later, that continue to dominate.

The Stop the Game campaign, meanwhile, published an open letter on Monday, signed by over 100 sporting figures, calling for the players not to fulfil the fixtures against Israel.

Ciara Mageean, Louise Quinn, Tony Ward, Joe Brolly and Colm O'Rourke were among the signatories. The letter claims pressure was being applied to the players after attempts to influence governing bodies and the government came to nought.

'The FAI, UEFA, and the Irish Government have all failed you by not taking decisive action and taking this out of your hands,' it claimed.

Sports.title: Gary Lineker labels Sir Jim Ratcliffe an 'unpleasant human being' in scathing attack on Man United co-owner - and congratulates the Glazers on 'finding someone even worse than them'
Sports.content:
Gary Lineker labels Sir Jim Ratcliffe an 'unpleasant human being' in scathing attack on Man United co-owner - and congratulates the Glazers on 'finding someone even worse than them'

Gary Lineker has delivered a scathing verdict on Sir Jim Ratcliffe's running of Manchester United, branding the club's co-owner an 'unpleasant human being'.

There was optimism when the 73-year-old bought a minority stake in the historic club in February 2024 and took control of football operations.

That mood now appears to have soured among sections of the fanbase, however, amid poor results on the pitch and growing frustration with decisions made under Ratcliffe's leadership.

Speaking on The Rest is Football podcast, England legend Lineker said: 'I look at Man United and I see problems coming down from the top.

'I must congratulate the Glazers on finding someone even worse than them that they can blame and getting him in there and getting all the stick: Jim Ratcliffe.

'I don’t think he’s a particularly pleasant human being and it’s a bit of a shambles of a football club the way it’s being run at the moment. So, well done to the Glazers on that one, deflecting everything away from them!'

'I must congratulate the Glazers on finding someone even worse than them that they can blame and getting him in there and getting all the stick: Jim Ratcliffe,' Lineker said

United fans protested against the club's ownership ahead of and during the Man City derby

United have already parted company with two permanent managers since Ratcliffe took charge of football operations. Erik ten Hag was sacked three months after being handed a new deal in October 2024, while his replacement, Ruben Amorim, departed in January this year after 14 months in charge.

Michael Carrick was appointed permanent manager in the summer after impressing in an interim role, recording 11 wins and three draws from 16 matches to steer the club back into the Champions League, but an underwhelming transfer window followed.

United missed out on targets Elliot Anderson and Matheus Fernandes, while they head into the international break in 12th place with just five points from their opening five games of the season.

In the last week academy starlet JJ Gabriel, nicknamed 'Kid Messi', has requested to leave the club due to his family's view that it has fallen behind the heavyweights of European football.

Daily Mail Sport has reported that a source close to the family explained that United are 'far away' from the likes of Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich as well as domestic rivals Arsenal and Manchester City, and that they want him to 'learn from the best' to maximise his talents.

Away from the pitch, Ratcliffe has been much-maligned for mass staff redundancies as well as increasing match ticket prices and season-ticket relocations in order to accommodate further hospitality seating. Ratcliffe also plans to build a new 100,000-seater stadium.

Fans protested against United's ownership ahead of and during September's Manchester derby defeat, and supporters' groups have called on Ratcliffe to resign over his recent comments on immigration.

Lineker added: 'It is a bit of a mess, that club. You've got a ground that's falling apart, all sorts of complaints about various things.

Join the discussion Is Manchester United's decline a failure of leadership or deeper club problems?

He congratulated the unpopular Glazers on finding Ratcliffe - 'someone even worse than them'

Talented youngster JJ Gabriel, nicknamed 'Kid Messi', has requested to leave the club due to his family's view that it has fallen behind the heavyweights of European football

'They're losing young teenagers, it looks like that (Gabriel leaving) is going to happen.

'The results, the inconsistency seems to be back. They have backed the manager many times and it’s not worked for them but there’s got to be something dripping down from the top.'

Previously, Ratcliffe has said that excessive criticism would cause him to walk away from the club if he was 'abused' by fans in the same way the Glazer family have.

The unpopular Glazer family bought the club in 2005 via a leveraged takeover and retain a majority stake.

'I mean, I can put up with it for a while,' Ratcliffe said in March. 'I don't mind being unpopular because I get that nobody likes seeing Manchester United down where they are, and nobody likes the decisions we're having to make at the moment.

'If I draw a bit of the ire, I can put up with that. But I'm no different to the average person. It's not nice, particularly for friends and family.

'So, eventually, if it reached the extent that the Glazer family have been abused, then I'd have to say, look, enough's enough guys, let somebody else do this.

'They can't really come to a match, the Glazers. They've retreated into the shadows a bit now, so I'm getting all the stick.'

Sports.title: 'I thought my ankle was going to snap': Andros Townsend speaks for first time on 'terrifying' moment he was RUN OVER by a pitch rolling machine at half-time during match in Thailand
Sports.content:
Ex-Premier League star Andros Townsend has admitted he was extremely fortunate to escape unscathed after being run over by a pitch roller in Thailand. The former England international, who joined Thai Premier League outfit PT Prachuap during the summer transfer window, looked to have suffered a freak injury when a manned pitch roller ploughed into him as he warmed up at half-time against Pattani. Footage of the incident quickly went viral on social media, but Townsend later made light of the ordeal on his Instagram story, posting: 'It turns out Stoke away wasn't so bad after all. Swipe to see why.' Remarkably, the former Crystal Palace winger was able to walk away from the incident unharmed and even came on as a second-half substitute. Appearing on Piers Morgan's Football Uncensored on Monday night, Townsend admitted it was a 'terrifying' experience but is very grateful to have escaped with only a few 'bumps and bruises'. 'I didn't see it coming,' he said. 'It was at halftime, we were going out to warm up. I saw two rollers on either side of the pitch. 🚨Andros Townsend got lucky to avoid injury during warmups in the Thai League pic.twitter.com/ctEOycMZcF — Polymarket Sports (@PolymarketSport) September 19, 2026 Former Premier League winger Andros Townsend has admitted he was extremely fortunate to escape unscathed after being run over by a pitch roller in Thailand on Saturday 'I remember thinking to myself, "I've never seen that before in my career, what are they doing?" But we got called to warm up. Didn't think anything of it. 'The next I saw him was when I was literally underneath him and thankfully no serious damage. A couple of bumps and bruises but managed to walk away unscathed, luckily. 'Every time I see it, I'm cringing, I'm in disbelief. When I sent it to my kids, my kids thought it was AI. Literally, I had to explain to them, for the next ten minutes, that it was real. 'It's horrible to watch back and to see what could have been but, like I said, thankfully I was fortunate I did manage to fall onto the floor at the right time, so nothing snapped as the roller went over me. And I'm here today to laugh about and tell the story.' As host Morgan pointed out, Townsend's team-mates reacted in horror as the roller mowed him down, fearing the worst for the former Premier League man. Footage showed the driver of the roller struggling to control the vehicle, with Townsend kicking a ball away, not looking in that direction. 'They (my team-mates) were very surprised that I continued the warm up! They were telling me to go to the doctor. They were calling for the stretcher. But listen, I've been around the block, I've had my setbacks, I've had my injury issues. A roller is definitely not going to stop me from continuing, that's for sure, so I was able to carry on. 'It was quite heavy, but I was able to kind of lift [it], force it off me. So when it was completely on me, I was getting crushed a little bit. 'But I was able to push it up, as you can see, as it falls on me, I was able to get my left arm up and relieve some of the pressure… and then I was able to get my team-mates around me who were able to lift it, and I was able to squeeze out but at that moment where it was crushing my left leg, it was quite terrifying, I must say. Townsend was bizarrely run over while warming up for a game at this new club in Thailand 'I was thinking I was done because it was my ankle, which I've had operated on. It was up my left knee, which I've had operated on. So I thought, either my left ankle was going to snap or my left knee is going to snap. I thought I was done. I was very fortunate that I was able to hobble away and recover within a few minutes.' PT Prachuap - based in Prachuap Khiri Khan province, 150 miles south of Bangkok - appeared to have leaked Townsend's arrival two weeks before he joined when they asked if anyone had a three-bedroom house available for the player to live in. They are the 17th club of his career. Townsend made 29 appearances for Kanchanaburi Power last season, scoring three goals. He has previously played for Spurs, Newcastle, Palace and Everton, and moved to Thailand after a short spell with Turkish side Antalyaspor. Townsend making the move comes after he worked for ITV as a co-commentator during the World Cup. The ex-England winger went viral at the tournament for his unconventional diet - which includes eating raw steak. He released a slew of videos promoting his all-natural diet including steak, sardines and boiled eggs.

Sports.title: Paul Merson questions Mikel Arteta's decision to start £75m ace Bruno Guimaraes ahead of Myles Lewis-Skelly in Brighton rout
Sports.content:
Paul Merson questions Mikel Arteta's decision to start £75m ace Bruno Guimaraes ahead of Myles Lewis-Skelly in Brighton rout

Paul Merson believes Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta made a mistake in starting Bruno Guimaraes against Brighton.

The Brazilian midfielder struggled – along with the rest of his team-mates – as the Gunners were soundly beaten 3-0 on the south coast.

'I’d like to ask Mikel Arteta what his thinking was behind playing Bruno Guimaraes over Myles Lewis-Skelly,' wrote former Arsenal forward Merson in his Sky Sports column.

'I don’t know if he thought it would be a nice football match, that Brighton would be tired after coming from 2-0 down against Manchester United on Wednesday?

'It just didn’t work. Arsenal got outrun, they got overpowered in midfield, they got ripped to shreds.

'Bruno’s a good footballer. If you’re playing a low block, I don’t see the problem in playing him. When you’re going to dominate the ball, there’s no-one like him when you have time. He’s a good player and passer – and he’s very intelligent.

Guimaraes struggled – along with the rest of his team-mates – as the Gunners were soundly beaten 3-0 on the south coast

'I just wonder if Arteta was sitting on the coach on the way back thinking "I’ve got that one wrong".

'When Bruno came on as a sub against Aston Villa a few weeks ago, he was outstanding. He could just keep the ball, pop it around, play one-twos and play the game at his tempo. That would have been a better idea.

'I’m not blaming Bruno for Arsenal losing, absolutely not. I just didn’t know why Arteta had to change the team in a very difficult game.'

Saturday's defeat left the defending champions second in the table after Manchester City followed up by beating Sunderland on Sunday to clinch the top spot with a three-point margin.

Sports.title: Baseball star left with brutal injuries after being struck in the FACE by foul ball
Sports.content:
Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman has suffered multiple facial fractures after being bludgeoned in the face with a foul ball during Sunday’s 9-1 win over the Reds in Cincinnati.

Bregman was standing several feet in front of the on-deck circle when he took a shot off teammate Michael Busch’s bat. Game footage showed Busch was actually checking his swing but nonetheless deflected the ball off the right side of the batter’s box and into Bregman’s left eye.

Although he immediately dropped his bat and went stumbling backwards, Bregman did not fall to the ground. Instead, he ran towards the Cubs dugout while holding his face before coming to a stop as trainers began to address his wound.

It was quickly decided that he needed to go to the clubhouse for a better evaluation, and he was seen being led down the dugout steps by trainers. Ultimately, he was taken to a Cincinnati-area hospital for X-rays and a CT scan.

Bregman responded shortly after the game on social media with a photo of his battered face. Not only was his black-and-blue eye firmly swollen shut, but the 32-year-old’s bloody nostril was stuffed with a specialized cotton nasal plug favorited by boxing cutmen.

‘Thanks for all the messages yall,’ Bregman wrote on Instagram. ‘I’ll be back.’

Alex Bregman was standing well in front of the on-deck circle when he was hit with the ball

Bregman initially ran towards the Cubs dugout while holding his face before coming to a stop as trainers began to address his wound. He was then removed from the game

Not only was Bregman's black-and-blue eye firmly swollen shut, but the 32-year-old’s bloody nostril was stuffed with a specialized cotton nasal plug favorited by boxing cutmen

Bregman's eye remained swollen shut above a patch of dried blood on his overgrown cheek

Due to the tests he received in Cincinnati, Bregman did not immediately travel with the Cubs back to Chicago. But when he did finally arrive back home, Bregman shared another photo of his face, which had only grown more swollen.

‘Back in Chicago,’ read the caption.

This time the tampon was out of Bregman’s nose, but his eye remained swollen shut above a patch of dried blood on his overgrown cheek.

ESPN's baseball insider Jeff Passan reported on Monday that while Bregman has several fractures, he will not undergo surgery and hopes to return for the playoffs.

Bregman arrived as a free agent after signing a five-year, $175 million deal with the Cubs following his 2025 season in Boston.

Best known for his years in Houston, Bregman initially struggled with the Cubs, but has seen his OPS (on-base percentage plus slugging percentage) jump from a disappointing .696 over the first half of the season to a robust .978 over his last 59 games.

For the year, Bregman has 26 home runs to go with a .262 average and .352 on-base percentage.

Sports.title: Tottenham plunged deeper into the mire as relegation chances soar, while Arsenal and Man City pull clear in two-horse title race: Supercomputer's updated Premier League predictions after five games
Sports.content:
Tottenham plunged deeper into the mire as relegation chances soar, while Arsenal and Man City pull clear in two-horse title race: Supercomputer's updated Premier League predictions after five games

The international break is here, giving Premier League clubs time to take stock of what has been a thrilling start to the 2026-27 season, and Opta to reevaluate their title predictions for the season's close.

We're only five games in and there are already a number of intriguing storylines developing, not least so-called relegation favourites Hull City's rampant return to the top flight after nine years away, claiming eight points to sit eighth heading into the break.

Enzo Maresca's start to life in charge of Manchester City couldn't have gone any better, winning all five games to clinch top spot as the only team with a 100 per cent record.

Brighton's stunning 3-0 defeat of Arsenal at the weekend has left the Premier League champions in second, while Fabian Hurzeler's side are next in line in third.

Only goal difference separates fourth to seventh in Brentford, Leeds, Liverpool and Everton, who each remain unbeaten so far.

Meanwhile, Chelsea are 10th with seven points, Michael Carrick's Manchester United are 12th and Tottenham, despite spending around £302million this summer, sit bottom of the table after collecting just two points. With Opta now giving them a 30 per cent chance of relegation, the outlook is already looking bleak for Roberto De Zerbi's side.

City's chances to win the title have increased considerably, closing the gap on Arsenal to 39.8 per cent, with Opta essentially predicting a two-horse race

To recap, Opta's supercomputer gave Arsenal a 40.6 per cent chance of retaining their title at the start of the campaign, making them favourites.

Manchester City were comfortably second favourites at 19.6 per cent, followed by Liverpool with 9.2 per cent and Manchester United with 6.6 per cent.

Interestingly, despite suffering that heavy defeat to the Seagulls at the weekend, Arsenal remain Opta's favourites to lift the trophy at the end of the season, with that percentage increasing to 43.7 per cent.

At the same time, City's chances have also increased considerably, closing the gap on Arsenal to 39.8 per cent, with Opta essentially predicting a two-horse race.

Liverpool are third favourites, but only with 5.7 per cent, that figure dropping slightly from the start of the season.

Brighton are now fourth favourites with 4.2 per cent. Brentford are fifth (1.2 per cent), Everton sixth (1.1 per cent) and Chelsea seventh (1.0 per cent).

Man United have struggled to put points on the board so far despite leading the Premier League for total shots (113) and touches in the opposition box (182). They have, as a result, fallen from fourth favourites at the beginning of the season to eighth, having just a 0.9 per cent chance of winning the title, the biggest fall of any team.

Aston Villa picked up their first win of the season against rock-bottom Spurs but lost three of their opening four matches and have been given just a 0.7 per cent chance of winning the title.

Join the discussion Should Spurs fans be furious about their club’s dramatic decline despite massive transfer spending?

Opta are giving Spurs a 30 per cent chance of relegation after their poor start to the season

And despite getting off to a strong start, Xabi Alonso's Chelsea side have now gone three games without a win and are given a 0.95 per cent chance of winning the title.

At the other end of the table, Coventry City, despite winning their first game of the season against Nottingham Forest at the weekend, are favourites to go down, with Opta giving them a 45.1 per cent chance of relegation.

Next in line for the drop are Alvaro Arbeloa's Fulham, who have a 42.4 per cent chance of relegation.

And finally, Roberto De Zerbi's Tottenham are third favourites to fall into the Championship at the end of the season, with the supercomputer having given them a 30 per cent chance of relegation.

Sports.title: Mo Salah handed six-month driving ban for speeding in his Rolls-Royce - just days after revealing his emotional Liverpool departure
Sports.content:
Mo Salah handed six-month driving ban for speeding in his Rolls-Royce - just days after revealing his emotional Liverpool departure

Former Liverpool footballer Mohamed Salah has been banned from driving for six months after his Rolls-Royce was clocked speeding.

The player failed to tell police who was at the wheel when the car was caught by a speed camera driving at 36mph on a 30mph stretch of road in Wilmslow, Cheshire, on March 27, according to court documents.

The 34-year-old did not respond to the notice of the prosecution, brought by Cheshire Constabulary, and did not enter a plea to the charge.

A court official said he was prosecuted at Warrington Combined Court under the Single Justice Procedure, which sees magistrates sit in private hearings, and was convicted of failing to give information relating to the identification of the driver of the Rolls Royce.

Salah has been banned from driving for six months after his Rolls-Royce was clocked speeding

The Egypt national captain was handed a six-month driving ban and ordered to pay £1,044, the court spokeswoman said.

The speeding offence came days after Salah announced he would be leaving Liverpool following nine years with the team.

Announcing his departure on March 24, the club said he had 'firmly established himself as one of the greatest players in Liverpool’s history'.

He scored 257 goals in 442 appearances for Liverpool, before transferring to Turkish side Trabzonspor following the 2025-26 season.

Sports.title: Paul Scholes accuses Man United of 'a lack of ambition' and 'buying players for the sake of it' - rather than trying to win the Premier League - and claims Michael Carrick will feel 'let down' by his bosses
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes accuses Man United of 'a lack of ambition' and 'buying players for the sake of it' - rather than trying to win the Premier League - and claims Michael Carrick will feel 'let down' by his bosses

Paul Scholes has claimed that Michael Carrick has been let down by the Manchester United hierarchy with their 'lack of ambition' over the summer.

United have managed to win just one of their opening five games of the season, a 5-2 victory over promoted side Ipswich Town. Otherwise, they have lost to Hull City and Manchester City, and have drawn against Everton and Fulham. They have also been knocked out of the Carabao Cup at the first time of asking.

United had a modest summer in the transfer market. With Casemiro leaving for Inter Miami and Manuel Ugarte - now injured - deemed not good enough, Elliot Anderson and Mateus Fernandes emerged as Carrick's top midfield targets. But Anderson joined Man City from Nottingham Forest in a £116million deal, while Fernandes chose Tottenham over United for £85m.

The club also considered Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, but baulked at the fees required to sign the pair, who eventually joined Spurs (£92.5m) and Arsenal (£75m) respectively.

Instead, United signed Carlos Baleba for £70million, though the Cameroon international is yet to feature after arriving with an ankle injury. Andrey Santos joined for £48m but has started only once, while Youri Tielemans arrived for £35m and Karl Darlow on a free transfer.

Carrick also wanted a new left back, but the club failed to provide cover or a long-term successor for the 31-year-old Luke Shaw.

Scholes has claimed that Carrick has been let down by the Manchester United hierarchy with their 'lack of ambition' over the summer

United have managed to win just one of their opening five games of the season, a 5-2 victory over promoted side Ipswich Town and have lost to Hull City and Manchester City

United legend Scholes has voiced his concern over the situation, with the club sitting in 12th after five games.

'It feels quite sad to say this but Man United are a club now that are not trying to win the league with recruitment,' he said on The Good, The Bat & The Football podcast.

'Santos, Baleba, they've brought players in that physically they may be better. Santos played 11 games for Chelsea, they paid £50million for him.

'But he's not getting into the team, now Baleba might make a bit of difference. But again, if you're recruiting at the start of the season for Manchester United, it should be for players that you think you can go and win the league with. I think they're a million miles away.

'I think they're just trying to consolidate from what Michael did last year, which is hard to get your head around. Were United trying to buy an Elliot Anderson? Probably. Now that's a signing where you think that might help you get a lot better. The players they've bought aren't making them any better.'

Centre-forward appears to be a particular sticking point for Scholes and his podcast partner Nicky Butt. United appeared willing to let forward Joshua Zirkzee leave the club in the summer, although a move failed to materialise.

Carrick has remained reluctant to play the Dutchman in Benjamin Sesko's absence and he has made just two substitute appearances in the Premier League so far, with Matheus Cunha getting the nod up top instead.

Butt said: 'Playing Cunha as a nine - it kills him, he's not a nine. He's nowhere near the player he is when he's playing off the side. We haven't got a number nine other than (Benjamin) Sesko. Zirkzee doesn't look anywhere near a Man United number nine. How can Man United have one centre forward that they can rely on?'

Carrick has been reluctant to play Zirkzee in Benjamin Sesko's absence and he has made just two substitute appearances in the Premier League

Carrick guided United to third in the Premier League last season, and both Scholes and Butt have claimed that Carrick has been let down by the club's hierarchy.

Scholes said: 'Michael must be really disappointed with what has happened in the summer. I reckon behind the scenes he thinks he's been let down. What Michael did last year was very, very good.

'The most important time for Michael was the start of this season. These games now are where you put a marker down, it gives you a foundation for the rest of the season.'

United have already seen two managers depart since Sir Jim Ratcliffe's INEOS took over footballing operations in February 2024. Erik ten Hag was sacked three months after being handed a new deal in October 2024. His replacement, Ruben Amorim, was then sacked in January this year after 14 months in charge.

Butt said: 'As a fan, the bit that gets me, I no longer think "it's a no-brainer we're going to win this game". Who can you point the finger at, and for me, it has to be the people upstairs that are pointing the people into place to pick the managers, the players, the coaches.

'I don't understand it. (Omar) Berrada the CEO said they're going to win the league by 2028. That's never going to happen the way it's going, never in a million years.

'I don't understand it. (Omar) Berrada the CEO said they're going to win the league by 2028. That's never going to happen the way it's going, never in a million years,' Butt said

'Without literally ripping them to shreds, it has to be said they've come in, they gave Ten Hag an extra few years on his contract, that didn't work. They went and got two other managers after that and it's still not working.

'There's got to be a real question being asked - is it being run right off the pitch, in recruitment and then that translates onto the pitch. So it's a massive big problem I think.'

Scholes added: 'I don't think we can keep blaming managers all the time. You can't just keep going through managers like we are doing. Recruitment will have an awful lot to answer for, especially after this summer.

'Are they looking at these top targets, Morgan Rogers, Elliot Anderson? It feels like we're buying players just for the sake of it. It feels like they're settling for third, fourth, fifth-best signings - and that isn't good enough. I'd rather just keep the money, and say "sure we can find someone in the academy who can do what these lads are doing".'

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino sets out big FIFA changes in new letter after backlash and quit calls
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino sets out big FIFA changes in new letter after backlash and quit calls

FIFA have come under immense pressure from member associations amid a controversial 12 months - but Gianni Infantino is desperate to cling on to power

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has written to FIFA members expressing an openness to reform at the organisation amid criticism. (Image: Getty Images)

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has agreed to commission an independent review as pressure mounts on his leadership. The supremo has been widely criticised following his plans to sell a 20 per cent stake in the organisation's commercial rights, including the World Cup, to investors in the latest controversy surrounding the chief.

‌



Infantino is said to have written to powers within the football sphere expressing an openness to talks about FIFA reform ahead of a meeting of the Council next month. The Swiss came under fire after hastily scrapping FIFA's Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, when members of the organisation publicly denounced the plans and Infantino's leadership.

‌



It is widely expected that the 56-year-old will be unchallenged in the next process to lead FIFA during March's election, but he has faced significant pressure to stand down from his role after the botched plan.

‌



JJ Gabriel's Man Utd transfer request explained by Wayne Rooney and Max Dowman comparison READ MORE :

Infantino has now written to member associations, offering an olive branch, as he said he will ask the council whether they want to launch an "independent external review of FIFA's current governance framework for major strategic initiatives and recommend potential improvements".

Proposals on the role of the president would be included, as well as "practical ways to strengthen transparency, participation and accountability in major strategic initiatives".

‌



Infantino, however, is keen to cling on to power, saying: "I remain fully committed to leading FIFA and confident in what we can achieve together."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The 56-year-old doubled down on the controversy surrounding a World Cup sell-off and external investment, insisting the FFE plan "did not involve relinquishing Fifa's control or authority over sporting decisions". He also claimed that "democratic processes, independence and sporting authority were never for sale. They are not for sale and never will be."

‌



He added: "The recent proposal explored whether a minority investment in a FIFA-controlled commercial company could generate additional resources for that purpose...

"The proposal entered the public domain before FIFA’s planned institutional process had been completed and before it could be presented in full to the Council and the Member Associations.

"I recognise that, without the full context, this caused concern and created the impression that decisions had already been taken. They had not.

‌



View 2 Images Gianni Infantino faced a boycott over his World Cup plans (Image: PA Wire)

"It remained a proposal, not a decision, and was always subject to the necessary approvals of the Council and the Member Associations. It has now been withdrawn and will not proceed.

"This experience has reinforced a simple point: a worthwhile objective must be matched by a process that commands confidence. Major ideas must be developed, tested and communicated through clear and trusted institutions. That is a responsibility I take seriously.

Article continues below

"The withdrawal of this proposal does not diminish our ambition or our responsibility to invest more of FIFA’s success back into football. We will continue to explore sustainable ways to grow FIFA’s resources and expand development and solidarity support for every Member Association. What changes is not the ambition, but the strength of the process through which major ideas are developed, tested and decided."

Infantino's letter comes after FIFA were called on by UEFA and CONCACAF - the confederations for Europe and North America, Central America, and the Caribbean - to pay £ 7.5 million to all 211 members in response to the president's aborted private equity proposal.

The 56-year-old, who has served as FIFA president since 2016, will stand for election for a fourth time in March 2027. His opponents will have until 18 November to find an alternative candidate.

Sports.title: Five Premier League questions that need answers as Man Utd flop and Arsenal defeated
Sports.content:
Five Premier League questions that need answers as Man Utd flop and Arsenal defeated

At the first international break Manchester City sit top of the Premier League after a shock loss for Arsenal whilst Manchester United and Tottenham have been massive disappointments

View 5 Images Manchester City have made a flying start to the season and sit top going into the international break (Image: Matt McNulty/Getty Images)

And breathe. The Premier League pauses for the first time as we embark on the international break, with England taking centre stage.

‌



Manchester City can enjoy a prolonged period at the top, owing to their 100 per cent record, the only one left in the top flight after Arsenal's loss on Saturday.

‌



In ways, the table has adopted a very familiar look - and in other ways not. Arsenal and City have been the top two in three of the last four seasons, and again occupy those positions. But Manchester United, Tottenham, Liverpool, Aston Villa and Chelsea will have expected more.

‌



Some of those managers are more under pressure than others. Some of those teams look like they will come good more than others. But all have managers with hefty expectations.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Hull City tasting defeat for the first time at the weekend sums up their impressive start. Ipswich, with two wins from five, will be happy enough with their early rounds.

The international break allows those involved in the domestic game to take stock. There's a blend of over performers and under performers with some facing more questions than other. Mirror Football takes a look at some of the discussion points around the Premier League before things resume on October 10 at the Emirates.

Was Arsenal's loss a blip?

And so that team who had been almost handed the title by some after just four games were bought back down to earth with a bang at Brighton. Arsenal's perfect record was ended by the Seagulls, who recorded a 3-0 win as the champions were downed for the first time this season.

‌



The Gunners, off the back of finally getting over the line last season, have played with a style that we didn't necessarily see last year, when the perception was that they relied excessively on set pieces.

View 5 Images Arsenal suffered their first defeat of the season at Brighton (Image: Getty)

Losing at the Amex allowed City to take early control at the top, leading Arsenal by three points. There's few question marks hanging over Mikel Arteta's side, their lack of elite star quality in the final third perhaps the only one.

‌



The manner of their loss could provide something of a blueprint for other teams to follow, but the likelihood is the Brighton loss was a bad day at the office and won't halt another title charge from the north Londoners.

Can Carrick turn things around at Man Utd?

This is all starting to feel concerningly like the autumn of 2021, which ended with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer getting the boot. A former player who got the job in surprise circumstances off the back of an interim spell no one expected. Sound familiar?

United were warned about repeating the trick but it seems they didn't heed the warning and one win from five games, leaving them in the bottom half, is not an ideal start for Michael Carrick in his first full season at the helm. There's not been much to hold onto either, their solitary win over Ipswich at Old Trafford.

‌



View 5 Images Michael Carrick has presided over a shocking start to the season (Image: Getty)

Defensively they look brittle and the decision not to invest in their backline, instead ploughing money into the midfield, looks a bad call after only a matter of weeks.

Ultimately, the manager is the man who will die on his sword. Gary Neville called out Carrick for letting his players off during post-match interviews, where he continues to give off a sense of positivity, even when a game has been a massive negative. The current United hierarchy have already sacked two managers in a relatively short time, but axing a third will call their judgement into question and further upset the fanbase. Results, though, could leave them with no choice.

‌



Is Isak really firing again?

The Golden Boot race has Erling Haaland sat top, shock, with the City star hitting five goals so far. A goal a game is pretty standard for the Norwegian nowadays as he chases his fourth Golden Boot in five years.

But the man keeping him honest right now on four goals: one Alexander Isak. Ridiculed in his first season at Liverpool, which was certainly injury-hit, the Swede is finding the back of the net even if his performance levels aren't necessarily matching those of his Newcastle days.

View 5 Images Only Erling Haaland has scored more goals than Alexander Isak this season (Image: Glyn KIRK/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



The winner at Bournemouth was his most recent strike, and his exploits in the final third are coming despite continued criticism of some of his team-mates. With a £125million price tag hanging over him it is about time Isak began delivering and his goals are keeping the critics as bad as Andoni Iraola gets his feet under the table.

Are Tottenham as bad as the league table suggests?

Five games gone. No wins. Bottom of the pile. After successive seasons where they finished 17th Tottenham fans must've thought the pain was over, but no. Even a manager with a big reputation and £300m worth of new signings hasn't changed anything.

It took them until the latter stages of their fifth games another home loss, to even score a goal. Ultimately, their two points from five games has been a fair reflection of what they are. It isn't as if they're losing games but playing well, or giving fans something to hold onto. Even their signings, which at the time had promise, now look questionable.

‌



Two former City players who were on the outers at the Etihad and an £85m midfielder who has been relegated for two years on the bounce. The consensus before a ball was kicked was that several good players under a manager who was lauded by the likes of Pep Guardiola must eventually click into gear and come good, but don't hold onto your hat given what we've seen so far.

View 5 Images Roberto De Zerbi and Tottenham look like a team lacking in ideas (Image: Getty Images)

Will Brighton and Brentford last the course?

With several of the group formerly known as the top six, the likes of Tottenham and the Red Devils, struggling, that has opened the door for others to prosper.

Article continues below

There's no doubt that Brighton and Brentford have been two of the best run clubs in the Premier League for years, and this could finally be the year they see the fruits of their labour. Their buy cheap, sell for big profit model hasn't hampered them, with their scouting top tier.

Both have already claimed scalps this season. Brighton downing Arsenal and Brentford getting the better of Chelsea - both doing so by three-goal margins. The Seagulls have had a taste of Europe, the Bees are yet to have their moment, but there's certainly a scenario come May that has both clubs inside the top seven.

Sports.title: Michael Vaughan fires warning to England batters after missing golden opportunity
Sports.content:
Michael Vaughan fires warning to England batters after missing golden opportunity

Emilio Gay, Dan Lawrence and Jordan Cox all showed flashes of promise during England’s 3-0 series whitewash against Pakistan, but Vaughan feels none did enough to completely remove themselves from the selection debate ahead of the winter tour.

View 2 Images Michael Vaughan at the launch of the Barclays Knight-Stokes Cup

Michael Vaughan believes England’s fringe Test batters have missed a golden opportunity to nail down their places before a far sterner examination in South Africa.

‌



Emilio Gay, Dan Lawrence and Jordan Cox all showed flashes of promise during England’s 3-0 series whitewash against Pakistan, but Vaughan feels none did enough to completely remove themselves from the selection debate ahead of the winter tour.

‌



The former England captain believes the trio will look back at the series and wonder whether they should have converted their promising starts into the big scores that would have almost certainly confirmed their place come the first Test against the reigning World Test Championship champions.

‌



Vaughan, speaking at Lord’s during the first-ever finals day of the Barclays Knight-Stokes Cup, said: “Test cricket is a little bit of a roller coaster. The one thing I’d say is, I think there’s been a few opportunities in this series for players to go and get big scores, and they haven’t taken them.

“I always say that when you get the opportunity against attacks – and it’s not disrespecting the Pakistani attack, but it’s not first-rate – make sure that you put a number in the bank, because when you come up against Rabada, Jansen and co. in South Africa, and Cummins and Hazlewood and Starc next summer, there are going to be more difficult days than we’ve seen in recent weeks. So, I’d have wanted big numbers if I’d have been an England batter.”

View 2 Images Altrincham Grammar School boys celebrate winning the inaugural Barclays Knight-Stokes Cup (Image: Jed Leicester/MCC)

‌



Gay, who has made three fifties in his first six Tests, did manage a valuable 60 in the third Test at Edgbaston, while Lawrence, who returned to the red-ball fold for the first time since 2024 in the first Test against Pakistan, made three half-centuries across the series. Cox, meanwhile, also made a trio of fifties against Pakistan, including an unbeaten 59 to help England chase down 130 in the third Test and seal a clean sweep.

But all three men missed out on the chance to push on and score three figures, and Vaughan expects Cox to be the unlucky man when Jacob Bethell returns.

“I like Jordan Cox. I think he’s a wonderful cricketer. I think he’s going to have a long England career, but you would think that Jacob would come back in at number three and that’ll be the only change,” he said.

‌



“I think Emilio Gay did enough. He’s opened the batting and he’s got three fifties inside his first six games. He’d have liked to have got three figures individually, but that hasn’t been the case. I would think he’ll certainly start in South Africa.

“I like this formula we’ve got at number six too. Lawrence is a player who has obviously gone away from his experience with England, come back a better player and looks the kind of player that I like to come in at number six.”

England now head into a daunting run of Test cricket, beginning with a three-match series in South Africa which will be new Test boss Stephen Fleming’s first in charge. The first Test is at the Wanderers in Johannesburg from December 17-21, followed by Tests at Centurion and Cape Town.

‌



They then travel to Australia in March for the 150th Anniversary Test before returning home for a blockbuster summer that includes a Test against Bangladesh at Lord’s in late May before the 2027 Ashes. And Vaughan thinks that schedule will quickly reveal whether England’s new-look batting order is ready for the biggest challenges.

“South Africa are a good side. They are the Test Championship winners and they’re in their own backyard. So that’s not going to be easy,” he added. "We’ll find out a lot more about the team, how much they’ve kind of moved on from the Ben Stokes and Baz McCullum era.”

Vaughan was speaking at the final of the Barclays Knight-Stokes Cup, which was held at Lord's in front of 2,000 people. The nationwide state school competition was the brainchild of the former England captain and saw Altrincham Grammar School and Chelmsford County High School for Girls lift the boys and girls trophies respectively.

Article continues below

“The Barclays Knight-Stokes Cup has been a huge success,” said Vaughan. “The standard has been great, the enthusiasm for the tournament has been amazing. It just proves to you that there is a real want for cricket in the state sector. They just need an opportunity. They need tournaments like this."

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Two Andoni Iraola transfer reunions proposed as Bradley Barcola sent message
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Two Andoni Iraola transfer reunions proposed as Bradley Barcola sent message

Liverpool are all smiles as they enter the international break

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola remains unbeaten as Liverpool boss (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

Liverpool's narrow 1-0 victory over Bournemouth will have left Andoni Iraola feeling positive about the start to his stint in charge. The Reds rose to sixth in the Premier League table after Sunday's win and remain one of just five unbeaten teams in the top flight.

‌



The Spaniard has led Liverpool to two wins and three draws thus far, while defeating Atletico Madrid and Tottenham Hotspur in the Champions League and Carabao Cup, respectively.

‌



The first international break of the campaign is now underway and Iraola has already been tipped to add to his squad by signing former favourites of his. Meanwhile, Bradley Barcola has been given a message from a Premier League icon.

‌



Mirror Football takes a look at the latest stories surrounding the Merseyside giants...

Iraola tipped to sign former stars

Jamie Carragher talked up the suggestion of Iraola raiding former club Bournemouth to sign Alex Scott and Rayan. The Spaniard enjoyed an impressive three-year stint on the south coast and led the club to European qualification last season for the first time, with the Cherries duo playing a huge role in the achievement.

Scott and Rayan were both linked with moves away in the summer, with the Englishman reportedly subject to interest from Manchester United and Arsenal. The Brazil international had been touted as a possible replacement for Mohamed Salah at Anfield, but both remained at the Vitality Stadium.

‌



Jamie Carragher speaks his mind on Florian Wirtz in damning verdict on Liverpool struggles READ MORE :

Andoni Iraola launches Florian Wirtz defence after stinging Jamie Carragher criticism READ MORE :

Carragher suggested on Sky Sports that Iraola may use his connection to prise them away from Bournemouth. The Reds legend said of Scott: "I think he’s a wonderful player. There was a lot of interest in him in the summer and because Liverpool have a former Bournemouth manager, you almost think: will there be a link or will there be a couple of players moving that way?

"I thought Rayan was fantastic last season as well. It will have been really good for him to get a goal in midweek because he probably hasn’t been himself at the start of the season. There are some fantastic players here at Bournemouth."

View 3 Images Bournemouth duo Alex Scott and Rayan were linked with moves away this past summer (Image: AFC Bournemouth via Getty Images)

‌



Shearer praises Barcola

Bradley Barcola became Liverpool's second-most expensive player ever last month when signing from Paris Saint-Germain in a £123million deal. The 23-year-old has yet to get off the mark in terms of goals and assists, but that hasn't stopped Alan Shearer from predicting Barcola to soon become a fan favourite at Anfield.

The Frenchman has started the last two Premier League games and has earned plaudits from the Newcastle icon, who believes he can become a "complete player" - but only if he adds more goals to his game. He recently told Betfair: "When Barcola started last week against Fulham, I thought he was brilliant.

View 3 Images Bradley Barcola has been praised by Alan Shearer (Image: AP Photo/Ian Walton)

Article continues below

"There is no doubt he's got huge ability. He needs to add more goals to his game to be complete. But in terms of excitement and getting people off their seat, he'll do that in abundance."

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Declan Rice red card verdict as two stars miss out on international action
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Declan Rice red card verdict as two stars miss out on international action

An extended international break is on the way and Arsenal can use the time to take stock after a difficult weekend in the Premier League

View 2 Images Declan Rice and Arsenal had a weekend to forget as they head into a three-week break (Image: Luke Hastings/Wired Photos/Shutterstock)

Arsenal have three weeks to lick their wounds after tasting defeat for the first time this season. The reigning Premier League champions were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and won't return to action until Leeds United come to the Emirates Stadium on October 10.

‌



It was a frustrating afternoon for the Gunners at the Amex Stadium as goals from Pascal Gross, Charalampos Kostoulas and Chema Andres gave Brighton all three points. It could have been even worse, with Declan Rice escaping a red card for an off-the-ball incident.

‌



Now it's time for an extended international break, during which some squad members could end up featuring in as many as four matches. Mikel Arteta will hope everyone comes back unscathed heading into a busy October.

‌



Not everyone will be away on international duty, as you'll soon learn, while there has been some more fallout from that Rice incident. Here are our latest lines from around the Emirates Stadium.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Atletico Madrid star hands Arsenal update on Julian Alvarez transfer READ MORE :

Arsenal sent JJ Gabriel transfer warning after Man Utd exit demand READ MORE :

Rice red card verdict

Declan Rice escaped punishment after kicking out at Brighton midfielder Malick Yalcouye during added time in Saturday's defeat. However, after pundit Alan Shearer said he doesn't believe it was sufficient for a red card, former Premier League official Dermot Gallagher has concurred.

‌



"I think it's petulant. What you've got to remember is that it's got to be deemed violent conduct," Gallagher said during an appearance on Sky Sports' Ref Watch.

"Is that brutal or malicious? I think not. He runs a risk, there's no doubt about that. For me, that's not an act of violence. It's a very unwise thing to do, but the referee got it right."

International absences announced

While many of his Arsenal team-mates head off on international duty, Piero Hincapie will stay at home. He is one of a number of high-profile absentees from the Ecuador squad, along with Chelsea's Moises Caicedo and Joel Ordonez of Club Brugge.

‌



View 2 Images Piero Hincapie won't link up with his Ecuador colleagues this month (Image: Xinhua/Shutterstock)

According to reports in South America, 'injuries and physical issues' are to blame for the trio missing out. Hincapie was an unused substitute for Arsenal at Brighton on Saturday but hasn't made it onto the pitch since the Champions League meeting with Napoli on September 9.

Ecuador face South Korea on September 24 in the first of three matches during this international break. This is the players' first chance to impress new manager Marcelo Gallardo, who replaced Sebastian Beccacece after the World Cup.

Article continues below

Hincapie's club team-mate Rice will also miss the upcoming international break, with football.london suggesting this is for load management reasons. The England midfielder is one of five stars to withdraw from Thomas Tuchel's squad at the time of writing, with Chelsea's Cole Palmer among the others.
