World.title: President Hichilema eulogizes late Lt Gen Zuze
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema has described the late Lieutenant General, Peter Zuze (retired) as a soldier, pioneer, diplomat and patriot who dedicated the best years of his life to serving mother Zambia.

The President said Lt Gen. Zuze, who hailed from Nalopa village in Petauke District in Eastern Province joined the Zambia Air Force in 1965 and rose to the position of Air Commander in 1972.

President Hichilema revealed that Lt Gen Zuze became the second Commander of the combined Zambia National Defence Force and is credited for helping build the Zambia Air Force into the proud force it is today.

The President’s remarks were delivered on his behalf by Secretary to the Cabinet, Patrick Kangwa, during the funeral service for the late military Chief.

President Hichilema noted that the late Lt Gen Zuze later served the country with distinction as a diplomat in Canada, the United Kingdom and the United Nations, where he contributed to the fight for freedom in the region and the advancement of peace.

President Hichilema said Lt Gen Zuze’s journey from a small village to commanding the skies of Zambia and representing the country on the global stage is a reminder that no village is too small to raise a general.

The Head of State also noted that the country has lost a father, a family man, and an airman who defended Zambia’s skies and later advanced peace and freedom through diplomacy.

“His life was defined by discipline, courage, patriotism, and service above self, to our young people, the journey by General Zuze from Nalopa to the United Nations shows what education and above all, discipline and purpose can achieve, ” he said.

He said while Lt Gen Zuze’s uniform may now be folded, his name, service and example as an educated citizen will remain woven into the history of the nation.

“A life well lived, a life to be emulated, and a life full of passion for Mother Zambia,” the President stated.

President Hichilema conveyed condolences to Mrs Gertrude Zuze, his children, grandchildren and the entire Zuze family, thanking them for sharing him with the nation through many years of service.

He further called on men and women in uniform to honour his memory through discipline, professionalism and faithful service to the nation.

Zambia Air Force Commander, Lt Gen Oscar Nyoni noted that 1st March 1972 is a date that defines ZAF when a 29-year-old Zambian officer, Peter Zuze, was entrusted with command of a young Air Force at a critical stage of national development, becoming the first indigenous Air Commander.

“His appointment marked a decisive transition from colonial command to indigenous Zambian leadership, it demonstrated that Zambians were ready and capable of commanding and shaping their own defence institutions,” Lt Gen Nyoni said.

He added that every 1st March is commemorated as Zambia Air Force Day, in honour of that transition and the confidence the founding President, Dr Kenneth Kaunda, reposed in him.

‘’As Senior Air Staff Officer, he oversaw construction of key bases including Mumbwa and Mbala now as Samora Mashel air base and as commander he reorganized and numbered flying squadrons to give ZAF structure, capability and identity,’’ said Lt Gen Nyoni added.

Lt Gen Nyoni said ZAF has immortalised him by naming the former Lusaka Air Force Base as Peter Zuze Air Force Base.

First Army Commander, General Kingsley Chinkuli, who served alongside Lt Gen Zuze, said his contribution must be seen in the context of a particularly challenging period marked by liberation struggles, political instability and serious security threats in the region.

“His legacy is not simply the positions he held, but the contributions he and our generation made to the development of the Defence Force structures and capabilities that underpin the peace and security Zambians enjoy today,” Gen Chinkuli said.

He said it was fitting that Lt Gen Zuze was being accorded full military honors and national respect, but his passing leaves a responsibility to reflect on the plight of former service chiefs.

“For more than eight years, Lieutenant General Zuze faced serious medical and welfare challenges. The hardships he and his family experienced are real examples of the wider difficulties being faced by a number of former service chiefs who do not have a comprehensive and clearly defined framework of welfare and entitlements after leaving office,” he said.

“I speak not as an observer, but as one who has walked the same path. We served under the same flag, during the same difficult period,” said Gen Chinkuli.

Gen Chinkuli appealed to President Hichilema, through the Secretary to the Cabinet and the Ministers present, to urgently address welfare concerns for retired service chiefs and uniformed personnel.

“We would like to ask you to really look at the concerns and the difficulties that are faced by former service people. We have a number of issues which need to be looked into as quickly as possible because people are facing difficulties in continuing to live a happy life,” he said.

“We remain hopeful that His Excellency will intervene so that those of our generation who are now elderly can enjoy the dignity, care and entitlements that our years of service have earned. That would be a fitting way to honor not only the memory of Lt Gen Peter Zuze but also the service of those still with us,” he stated.

He however extended his condolences to Mrs Zuze and the family on behalf of fellow Service Chiefs.

“Lt Gen Zuze has completed his watch. He served his country. Indeed, his duty is done,” he added.

Meanwhile, wife to the late Getrude Zuze said she was married to him for 55 years stating that she enjoyed life with him as partner and friend.

Speaking through a family representative, Bridget Lupambo, Mrs Zuze described the late husband as a loving, dedicated family man who anchored their home with discipline, love, faith and humility despite demands of national duty.

Lt Gen Zuze is survived by a wife, 4 children and 2 grandchildren.

He died on 14th September 2026 and has since been put to rest at leopards Hill memorial park.

World.title: ‘You’ll Pay Heavily’ — Muhabi Warns Government Over Opposition Detentions
World.content:
‘You’ll Pay Heavily’ — Muhabi Warns Government Over Opposition Detentions

We Are One Zambia (WOZA) Secretary General Muhabi Lungu has warned that government will pay a heavy price for the continued detention of opposition leaders held at Mukobeko Maximum Security Prison on treason charges he described as trumped-up.

Speaking on Millennium Radio’s The Interview programme, Lungu said keeping the opposition in custody without trial was unlawful and would cost the nation dearly, both locally and on the international stage.

“Under systems that work, after my illegal detention, I was compensated by the state. All properties I own now are proceeds of that wrongful arrest,” Lungu said.

“My caution is simple. There will be a heavy price to pay for today’s illegal detentions of Brian Mundubile, Makebi Zulu and others.”

Those held include Mundubile, his running mate Zulu, retired Bishop Trevor Mwamba, lawyer George Chisanga, businessman Harry Valden Findlay, Patrick Mwansa, Davis Chisopa and a dozen others, all facing treason charges that carry no provision for bail.

Lungu said the United Nations and the European Union had both described the charges against the group as concocted. He said the UPND government’s handling of the matter had already dented the nation’s image abroad.

“Government is playing cat and mouse and thinks Zambians are idiots. You cannot incarcerate a person for challenging for a political position. This is unacceptable,” he said.

Lungu recalled his own detention 30 years ago on murder and treason charges. He was arrested at 29, appeared in court the next day, and was acquitted after three and a half months for lack of evidence.

“That is due process,” he said. He added that he was later compensated by the state for the wrongful arrest, and that the properties he owns today are proceeds of that compensation.

Lungu challenged Attorney General Mulilo Kabesha and Director of Public Prosecutions Gilbert Phiri to take those arrested to court without further delay.

“If you don’t have evidence, release them. The world is watching. You have embarrassed this nation so much. And now we have a leader who is scared to attend the United Nations General Assembly because of the backlash,” he said.

He also challenged Kabesha’s public claim that there was no evidence of malpractice surrounding the disputed presidential vote.

“Let Kabesha deny that Mundubile was abducted and released on 14 August. Let him deny that his friend Mutotwe Kafwaya was shot twice. The state first denied it, then admitted killing him only after his wife sought habeas corpus,” he said.

He questioned the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) over why it stopped counting for six hours after polling day, and why the courts were shut down at a critical moment, preventing the opposition from challenging the results.

“This is a very strange government with strange people leading us. First you investigate, gather evidence, then arrest. Don’t arrest first and probe later. Even a first-year law student knows this,” Lungu said.

He praised founding president Kenneth Kaunda for pardoning coup suspects Edward Shamwana and Christon Tembo without waiting for the courts to conclude their processes.

Lungu said Mundubile, Zulu, Bishop Mwamba and the others in custody remained in high spirits because they knew they were innocent.

“They are not militia. Take them to court or free them,” he said.The detainees have yet to be formally arraigned on the treason charges.

World.title: Ten Years Is Enough: Zambia Should Not Swap Its Term Limit for a Promise of Development
World.content:
Ten Years Is Enough: Zambia Should Not Swap Its Term Limit for a Promise of Development

A whisper is turning into a chorus. President Hichilema won a second term on August 13, and under the Constitution it is his last, ending in 2031. Yet a UPND MP has already argued that women want development rather than democracy and should back him to stay beyond 2031. Chilufya Tayali called the ten-year ceiling retrogressive and bad for Zambia. A party official has even argued that Hichilema’s two terms should only begin counting from 2031. None of this is government policy. But ideas floated as tests rarely stay floating.

The false choice

“Development, not democracy” sounds practical, but it treats the vote as a luxury. Elections and term limits are how a country corrects its mistakes. A leader who cannot be removed has little reason to listen when a road is badly built, a tender is rigged or a hospital runs out of drugs.

What our neighbours show

Uganda is the clearest warning. Museveni has ruled since 1986 and extended his stay by removing term limits in 2005 and the age limit in 2017. Reports say MPs received Shs5m each before voting to scrap the limits. He has now won a seventh term, with his son Muhoozi, the army chief, widely seen as being groomed to succeed him. An Afrobarometer survey found that most Ugandans want presidential term and age limits reinstated.

Zimbabwe shows the same appetite with a modern face. After a 2017 coup ended Mugabe’s near four decades in power, Mnangagwa signed a law extending his term to 2030, stretching presidential terms from five years to seven and ending direct election of future presidents, who will instead be chosen by Parliament. Supporters call it stability. Critics call it capture.

Rwanda, from my own knowledge, amended its constitution by referendum in 2015. Kagame can now stay in power until 2034, and he won the 2024 election with about 99% of the vote. A result like that reads more like a coronation than a contest.

The honest pluses

Fairness demands we acknowledge that long rule can deliver. Rwanda is clean, orderly and admired for its efficiency. Uganda’s ruler is praised for restoring stability, growing the economy and improving infrastructure. Continuity can protect long projects, whether mines, power plants or debt restructuring. And in principle, voters should decide how long a leader stays.

But look at the price. In Zimbabwe, the president stands accused of rampant corruption and suppressing rights while ordinary people endure hardship despite a growing economy. Development that depends on one man’s indefinite stay is fragile. When he goes, or tires, the system has no trained successors and no tradition of peaceful handover. Rwanda’s order is real, but so is the silence around it.

What it means for young Zambians

Zambia is a young country, and its young people are told to be patient. The presidency, which as far as I know requires a candidate to be at least 35, is already a distant summit. Remove the limit and the ladder gets shorter still. A 25-year-old today could reach 50 without ever seeing a fresh face at State House.

Hichilema himself is the best argument against the idea. He contested five presidential elections before winning in 2021. He got there because Zambia’s system allowed a defeated incumbent to concede and a persistent opponent to win. Take that possibility away and we close the door he walked through.

Elsewhere, alternation has become a source of pride. Ghana, Malawi and Botswana have all seen governing parties lose and leave peacefully, and Zambia’s own 2011 and 2021 handovers belong on that list. That record is worth more than any single term.

A better path

If the goal is stable development, strengthen institutions rather than personalities: an independent electoral commission, a free press, courts that can rule against the government, and space for the opposition. If the term limit must be debated, do it openly, through a referendum, and with one firm safeguard. In Zimbabwe, opponents argued that no amendment should benefit a sitting president. That principle protects everyone, whichever party is in power.

Bill 7 showed how quickly a large majority can move, since it cleared the two-thirds threshold required for constitutional changes. A big majority in the House is not the same as consent from the people. Let Zambians keep their five-year vote and their two-term limit. Leaders who deliver do not need more time. Their record is their campaign.

World.title: Africa: World Recognizing Africa as a 'Gamechanger for Global Business' - UN Chief
World.content:
Geneva — United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has told the Global Africa Business Initiative that Africa represents a $3 trillion market opportunity and the world is finally recognizing it as a “gamechanger for global business”.

He addressed the 5th initiative titled Unstoppable Africa on Sept. 20, saying, “We come together inspired by a simple truth: that Africa’s future must be shaped by Africans, for Africans. That vision is rapidly gaining momentum.”

Guterres noted in his address to the African Union chairperson that Africa has the world’s fastest-growing labour force, holds 30 percent of global mineral resources and 60 percent of the solar potential.

Financial markets are taking notice, and Africa’s fintech sector is now the continent’s largest draw for investment capital, he noted.



‘No more plundering’

Still, he said the world must ensure that Africa’s vast natural resources – particularly critical minerals – create local value and decent jobs, rather than simply being shipped overseas, and he said there should be “no more plundering”.

“In short, the shift you long envisioned is taking place: from doing business in Africa, to doing business with Africa.”

Africa is “home to a growing cohort of thought leaders and youth entrepreneurs,” said the UN chief at the New York event according to a release made in Geneva.

“We are here to deepen investments, empower dealmakers, and build genuine partnerships. And the signals of growth are strong.”

Africa booming in renewable energy field

In the essential field of renewable energy, Africa is booming, said Guterres.

He noted that Kenya now generates more than 90 percent of its electricity from renewable sources, while Morocco is developing plans for the Pont de la Méditerranée, a submarine cable to supply green electricity to Europe.

In the technology arena, Tunisia is competing globally in AI and computer vision software, and Rwanda is pioneering nationwide drone delivery.

“Africa’s star is also rising in the entertainment sector,” observed Guterres, with Nigeria, South Africa, and Senegal creating music and film for audiences across the globe.

Close 

“All this has financial markets taking notice,” the UN chief extolled. “Africa’s fintech sector is now the continent’s largest draw for investment capital.”

Trade under the African Continental Free Trade Area is on track to reach $230 billion in 2026.

Despite global turbulence, all the wars and problems facing the world, Africa’s economy grew 4.4 percent in 2025.

Headwinds intensifying

“But the headwinds are intensifying,” noted Guterres.

Without referring to U.S. President Donald Trump specifically, he said tariffs are less predictable.

“Competition over critical minerals is rising. And the conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East are reverberating through supply chains for fertilizers, food, and fuel,” he said, while costs are increasing along with interest rates.

“Yet these disruptions also create an opportunity: to move from economies that depend on exports, to value that stays and grows at home,” said the UN chief.

Guterres also observed that in the continent’s conflicts, it is vital that Africa takes ownership and bring local mediation to bear, as it has in Ethiopia and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

“And Africa also needs permanent seats on the United Nations Security Council, where it can contribute to dialogue and action for the whole globe,” he said.

World.title: Malawi: Malawi's Climate Fight 'Strangled' By Crushing Debt Burden, Actionaid Warns
World.content:
Malawi is being denied the chance to fight back against climate change because a staggering 24 percent of the national budget is being swallowed up by debt repayments, campaigners have warned.

ActionAid Malawi (AAM) Climate Justice Focal Chairperson Jimmy Chimalizeni made the explosive claim during an aerobics event the organisation jointly staged with fellow NGOs to rally young people ahead of the Global Week for Climate Justice.

Chimalizeni didn't mince his words, insisting Malawi simply cannot achieve climate justice while its finances remain shackled by debt.

He said the country's spiralling public debt is directly sabotaging the fight against climate change, with scarce cash that should be going towards climate action, health, education and agriculture instead being siphoned off to service loans.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

"This year during the Global Week for mobilisation for climate justice, the young people have been mobilised. Mostly, we are talking about the issues of debt cancellation," he said.

"We have calculated a very huge amount of public debt, and at this stage, its repayment has affected the allocation of other resources into other essential public services like health, education, and agriculture."

For ActionAid, the message is stark: climate justice and debt justice are two sides of the same coin.

According to the organisation's own figures, more than 24 percent of the national budget -- recorded in government books as public debt charges -- is now being funnelled into debt servicing, leaving climate financing scraping the barrel.

"The funds that are required to be channeled towards climate action now have been redirected to debt servicing. This has left other sectors like climate financing with very little resources," he said.

It's why, Chimalizeni explained, this year's youth-driven campaign is demanding not just climate action but outright debt cancellation and a shake-up of the global debt system.

Youth demand a seat at the table

Campaigners are also pushing back against the idea that young people are merely helpless bystanders in the climate crisis.

ActionAid wants them recognised as "agents of change" with a genuine say in decisions on climate policy.

"We are seeing young people not just as victims of climate change... but we are also seeing them as agents of change, so we want them to have a seat at the table, even on questions of climate and climate justice," Chimalizeni said.

Mining cash 'must reach communities'

With mining activity booming across Malawi, ActionAid is also demanding that proceeds from extraction be transparently redirected into climate financing -- and that communities living alongside mining operations actually see the benefit.

Chimalizeni said the timing couldn't be more critical, with world leaders set to gather for the UN General Assembly in October and COP30 in November, where Malawi's negotiators must make the case for debt-distressed, climate-vulnerable nations like itself.

'People know the answers -- they just need the money'

Pressed on what government and NGOs should actually do to tackle the root causes of climate vulnerability, from farming to energy poverty, Chimalizeni insisted the solutions already exist at grassroots level -- they're just starved of cash.

"Most of our interventions, they simply need funding. This is right from the communities where we work, where a lot of people are saying we believe that the solutions are just there. They just need funding," he said.

He singled out energy as an urgent priority, accusing authorities of telling Malawians to abandon firewood without giving them anything affordable to replace it with.

Close 

"We are telling people not to use firewood, but we are not giving them the other alternatives. Most of these energy sources are expensive," he said, calling for government subsidies on solar, gas and other clean energy sources.

He also warned that Malawi's heavy dependence on hydropower -- vulnerable to both drought and flooding -- leaves the country dangerously exposed, and renewed calls for a genuine, "just" transition to diversified energy sources.

"We need a proper transition. We need a just transition to other sources of energy. If we can allocate more resources towards these investments, I'm sure we can deal with the climate crisis," he said.

ActionAid's verdict is blunt: unless Malawi frees up fiscal space from crippling debt, empowers its youth, and ensures mining wealth actually funds climate resilience, the country will keep paying the price for a crisis it did almost nothing to cause.

World.title: Uganda: Alarm Bells for Kasese As Rivers Swell
World.content:
Heavy overnight rainfall has caused major rivers in Kasese District to swell, with River Nyamwamba bursting its banks and flooding communities in parts of Kasese Municipality.

The flooding has renewed concerns about the district's preparedness for heavier rainfall during the ongoing rainy season, particularly in communities along river channels, low-lying areas and other flood-prone locations.

Kasese lies at the foot of the Rwenzori Mountains, where heavy rainfall in the highlands can quickly increase water volumes flowing downstream through the district's major rivers.

Rivers Nyamwamba, Nyamugasani and Mubuku all recorded significant rises following the rains, with Nyamwamba overflowing its channel and affecting homes and property in several communities.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

Kasese Municipality Deputy Town Clerk Zedekiah Kayiri said some sections of Nyamwamba have weak points where water can easily escape its channel and reach nearby communities.

Kayiri called for accelerated intervention by the Ministry of Water and Environment to find a permanent solution to the recurring flooding along the river.

"The river has known weak points where water can break out of its channel and disrupt communities within the municipality, and therefore we ask the relevant Ministry to act swiftly towards River Nyamwamba," Kayiri said.

More than 80 houses were reportedly affected by the latest flooding, while at least 20 households were displaced.

Kasese District Disaster Focal Person Joseph Isingoma said the impact should serve as a warning to communities in vulnerable areas as more rainfall is expected.

"The latest rains left more than 80 houses affected while 20 households were displaced. This is a serious warning while more rains are still expected," Isingoma said.

Local leaders have urged residents living in high-risk areas to consider temporary relocation to safer places for the remainder of the rainy season.

Nyamwamba Division LCIII Chairperson Brian Kauntura asked residents in the most vulnerable areas to take precautionary measures rather than wait for floodwaters to reach their homes.

"I want to urge those living in areas of vulnerability to consider immediate relocation as we monitor the situation," Kauntura said.

The recurring floods have left communities along the river facing repeated threats to homes and property, while local authorities continue to rely largely on emergency measures when water levels rise.

Municipal authorities say a lasting solution will require addressing the points where Nyamwamba regularly breaks its banks and reducing the exposure of communities living in flood-prone areas.

Close 

With the rainy season continuing, residents have been urged to remain vigilant, monitor weather and disaster warnings and move to safer locations whenever advised.

The latest flooding has once again highlighted Kasese's exposure to extreme weather and the need for both immediate preparedness and longer-term measures to protect communities from rising flood risks.

World.title: Africa: AU, UN Reinforce Joint Commitments On Peace, Economy and Resource Equity
World.content:
Addis Ababa — The Chairperson of the African Union Commission, Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, and United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres have co-chaired a high-level AU-UN meeting on the margins of the 81st United Nations General Assembly to deepen strategic cooperation, strengthen peace and security frameworks, and advance global financial reforms in support of Africa.

According to a social media post by the AU, the meeting reaffirmed the two institutions' shared commitment to supporting Africa's efforts to address structural challenges and promote a fairer international order. Key issues discussed included reform of the international financial architecture, debt sustainability, and ensuring that African countries derive greater value from their critical mineral resources.

The two sides underscored the strategic importance of AU-UN cooperation, including the three existing cooperation frameworks, and the need to finalise the joint roadmap beyond 2026. The United Nations was reaffirmed as a key partner of the AU in addressing peace and security challenges on the continent.

On peace and security, the meeting highlighted the need to strengthen Africa's peace and security architecture, reinforce preventive diplomacy and mediation, and ensure adequate resources to support African-led solutions to African challenges.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The discussions also reviewed developments in the Sahel, Libya, Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, including continued support for the mediation led by Togo in the DRC.

The meeting further expressed concern over external shocks, including conflicts, disruptions to global supply chains, and maritime chokepoints, which are placing additional pressure on African economies and food security. The potential impact of climate-related events was also highlighted.

The two sides agreed on the need for concrete follow-up action, including finalising the AU-UN roadmap, planned engagements on Libya and Sudan, identifying countries most vulnerable to food insecurity, and developing contingency measures through strengthened coordination and financing.

World.title: Kenya: KNCHR Warns of Rising Insecurity, Political Violence Ahead of 2027
World.content:
Nairobi — The Kenya National Commission on Human Rights (KNCHR) has raised concerns over renewed insecurity in parts of the country and growing political violence and inflammatory rhetoric ahead of the 2027 General Election.

The Commission called for urgent investigations into recent killings in Isiolo and Embu, renewed attacks along the Turkana-West Pokot border, and alleged human rights abuses during security operations in Pokot Central.

KNCHR Chairperson Claris Ogangah said the State has a responsibility to protect the right to life and security regardless of a person's location, ethnicity or political affiliation.

"The right to life is not negotiable, and does not depend on geography, ethnicity, political affiliation or public prominence," Ogangah said.



The Commission warned that failure to address the concerns early could affect the rights to life, security, freedom of movement and political participation as the country approaches the 2027 elections.

KNCHR said insecurity had returned to sections of the Turkana-West Pokot border after a period of relative calm following disarmament and peacebuilding initiatives.

The Commission reported deaths, livestock theft and destruction of houses on both sides of the border.

Areas identified on the Turkana side include Kakong, Aroo and Lokwar/Nakuse, while Romos, Morita, Ompolion and Kases were among the affected areas in Pokot North.

KNCHR also raised concerns over an alleged security operation on September 17 in which residents of Nasolot and Sarmach in Pokot Central were reportedly assaulted and houses torched.

The Commission said the circumstances and motive of the alleged operation remained unclear and called for investigations.

It also cited a September 11 attack on a passenger vehicle near Kakong'u along the Lodwar-Kapenguria Highway, in which three passengers were reportedly injured.

According to KNCHR, the insecurity has broader consequences for education, healthcare, food security, property and freedom of movement.

The Commission identified women, children, older persons and people with disabilities as groups requiring particular protection.

While welcoming the work of multi-agency security teams, KNCHR called for stronger oversight of their operations.

In Isiolo, the Commission highlighted the September 16 killing of five people in Gotu in an alleged bandit attack.

The victims included two police officers and three elders who were reportedly part of a search party.

KNCHR also cited other recent incidents, including the reported shooting of a police constable during an ambush on an Anti-Stock Theft Unit patrol in Burat Ward and the reported killing of two people along the Meru-Isiolo border in August.

The Commission said the attacks were creating fear, disrupting livelihoods and undermining peace in the affected areas.

It called for sustained security interventions, including intelligence-led patrols, alongside accountability for those responsible for attacks.

The human rights body also raised concerns over violence reported at Nembure Grounds in Embu on September 12, where two people died and several others were injured.

The victims were identified as Mike Macharia, 23, and Moses Munene, 30.

KNCHR said postmortem examinations established that both men died from gunshot wounds.

The Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA) has opened an investigation into whether the use of force by police during the incident was necessary and proportionate.

KNCHR called for an impartial investigation and accountability for anyone found responsible.

"Political competition must be a contest of ideas, not an arena for violence," the Commission said.

KNCHR also expressed concern over political statements that it said could undermine peaceful political participation ahead of the 2027 elections.

The Commission cited remarks attributed to Mukurwe-ini MP John Kaguchia, nominated MP Joseph Wainaina Iraya and UDA Secretary-General Hassan Omar, noting that the matters are before the National Cohesion and Integration Commission (NCIC), the courts, or both.

KNCHR said statements perceived as threatening or excluding citizens because of their political choices could create fear and discourage people from participating freely in political activities.

It also cautioned that remarks appearing to trivialise electoral malpractice, even where later clarified, could undermine public confidence in democratic institutions.

The Commission noted that Article 38 of the Constitution protects political rights, while Article 81 requires elections to be free from violence, intimidation and improper influence.

It further pointed out that freedom of expression under Article 33 does not extend to incitement to violence.

KNCHR has called on the National Police Service, Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) and IPOA to promptly investigate reported violence in Embu and along the Turkana-West Pokot border.

Close 

It also wants disarmament operations targeting communities holding illegal firearms across the North Rift and the Isiolo-Marsabit-Samburu corridor to comply with human rights standards.

The Commission has proposed an oversight mechanism for multi-agency security teams involved in disarmament and patrol operations to ensure their actions remain lawful and proportionate.

It further wants the NCIC and DCI to investigate credible reports of incitement regardless of political affiliation.

County governments, religious and community leaders and civil society organisations have been urged to strengthen peacebuilding efforts and ensure affected communities continue accessing essential services.

Political parties and leaders have also been called upon to reject violence, intimidation and inflammatory rhetoric.

The latest warning follows previous KNCHR interventions on political violence. In August, the Commission condemned political intolerance, violence and the alleged use of organised groups during political activities, while in July it raised concerns over political violence and alleged electoral malpractice during campaigns for the Ol Kalou by-election.

KNCHR said protection of life and fundamental freedoms must begin before violence occurs.

"The time to protect life is before it is lost," the Commission said.

World.title: Giants' season-opening high comes crashing down as Jaxson Dart's knee injury overshadows Rams' blowout win
World.content:
The New York Giants were riding high coming into Los Angeles to face a frustrated Rams team that returned home from a beatdown in Australia.

After defeating the Dallas Cowboys on their own home turf, the talk around the league after just one week was that the Giants could be a problem for the rest of the NFL in this John Harbaugh era.

But those giant expectations took a massive hit on "Monday Night Football" after quarterback Jaxson Dart was ruled out after a brutal hit led to a knee injury that now has the organization and fan base collectively waiting for MRI results with bated breath.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Once Dart left the game, and Jameis Winston took over for the Giants, the offense that surprised the Cowboys last week with its ground-and-pound nature struggled to find its footing against a revitalized Rams defense—one that lacked Myles Garrett, but featured the return of future Hall of Fame defensive tackle Aaron Donald at SoFi Stadium.

Meanwhile, Matthew Stafford looked more like the reigning MVP in this game compared to Week 1, and with tons of time in the pocket, he dissected the Giants’ defense as the Rams cruised to a 28-6 victory to get its first of the new season.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Now, things hang in the balance as the Giants await Dart’s MRI results, which should come on Tuesday. Dart was clutching at his knee after getting sandwiched between two Rams defenders that beat the Giants’ tackles off the edge, and while airborne, video replay showed his leg shift in an awkward way.

Dart was able to walk off on his own power, and ESPN’s Jordan Raanan even reported during the game that he tried to let the coaching staff put him back in the game. They refused to let him.

It's a good sign to see Dart’s fight to get back in the game, which could also showcase that his injury isn’t as severe as initially thought. OutKick's Armando Salguero reported a possible MCL could be what Dart and the Giants are looking at, but in a Week 2 filled with key quarterback injuries, every party is just hoping the 2026 season isn't awash for the second-year signal caller out of Ole Miss.

If Dart is to miss time, this new Giants regime will be tested to keep their lofty expectations afloat because, after watching what occurred on both sides of the ball, there’s certainly work to do.

On offense, while it’s a tough task for any backup quarterback to take over on a moment’s notice, the run game that worked so well in Week 1 was non-existent this time around. It certainly helped that Donald was back in a Rams uniform, but the rest of their defenders were solid at the line of scrimmage, limiting New York to just 44 rushing yards as a team compared to 165 in Week 1. Donald finished his first game back in two years with three total tackles, one for loss.

It also didn't help the Giants that star receiver Malik Nabers gave the team a scare when he left after getting a target from Winston, gripping at his right shoulder. He would eventually return to the game, but occurring just a few snaps between Dart's injury, Giants fans were thinking the worst yet again.

AARON DONALD REVEALS WIFE'S ADVICE THAT HELPED HIM MAKE DECISION TO COME OUT OF RETIREMENT AND RE-JOIN RAMS

Then, on defense, Stafford didn’t have Puka Nacua, who was sidelined due to injury, but he did have future Hall of Fame receiver Davante Adams. With the Giants finding no amount of pressure on most of Stafford’s dropbacks, he couldn’t stop finding Adams for chunk plays.

It was a 31-yard touchdown pass to Adams for his first score of the game, a 64-yard catch-and-run set up a touchdown pass to running back Kyren Williams, and a signature fade route where Giants rookie cornerback Colton Hood had no chance after Adams’ release off the line. Adams finished the game with eight catches for 195 yards and two scores.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

The Giants' pass rush, which was expected to be a potentially fearsome group this season, will be a talking point throughout the week as Abdul Carter, Brian Burns, Kayvon Thibodeaux and more couldn't get through the Rams' offensive line, which held up nicely for their 38-year-old quarterback to operate. And the injury bug continued toward the end of the game for the Giants, as Burns rolled his ankle. The cart came out to take him to the locker room, but he turned it down to walk on his own.

It was a tail of two sidelines where the Rams got back on the right path, while the Giants, in the midst of hoping for the best for their quarterback, need to go back to the drawing board with crucial home games ahead.

World.title: Trump was a 'caged lion' roaring to return to WHCA Dinner ballroom after shooting, Leavitt says
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt revealed new details on President Donald Trump’s behind-the-scenes response after shots were fired at the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner in April.

Leavitt said in a new episode of "Hang Out with Sean Hannity" that Trump was behaving like a caged animal and was adamant about returning to the ballroom, despite having just narrowly escaped from an alleged assassination attempt.

"He was like a caged lion backstage, like just roaring to get out, like, 'We gotta go back out there,’" she said. "And I'm sitting there like, ‘I don't know if I want to go back out there.’"

TRUMP ADMITS HE 'WASN'T MAKING IT THAT EASY' FOR SECRET SERVICE DURING WHCD SHOOTING

Minutes after the WHCA Dinner began at the Washington Hilton, a gunman, later identified as Cole Allen of Torrance, Calif., allegedly stormed the hotel while armed with weapons. Trump and Vice President JD Vance were quickly escorted out of the ballroom by members of the Secret Service.

Allen, who was quickly apprehended by Secret Service agents, allegedly wrote in a manifesto that his targets were Trump administration officials except for FBI Director Kash Patel.

WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENTS' DINNER SHOOTING: TIMELINE TRACES HOW SUSPECT’S ALLEGED CROSS-COUNTRY PLAN UNFOLDED

Guests dived under tables as the gala, meant to celebrate White House correspondents, descended into chaos.

Yet, Leavitt said, the president was eager to return to the ballroom and willing to wait hours for the event to resume.

"[Trump] really was asking hard questions of his detail, like, ‘Why can't I go? I will wait all night. I don't care if it's 3 in the morning, get it started,’" Leavitt shared.

The former White House spokeswoman said officials even began making preparations to resume the dinner as she described Trump’s impatience to make a public statement immediately after the incident.

WHITE HOUSE CORRESPONDENTS' DINNER SHOOTING SHARPENS FOCUS ON TRUMP’S BALLROOM CONSTRUCTION PROPOSAL

"[Trump] wanted to say something and the best way to say it was in the briefing room. And we did," Leavitt said.

Trump held a news conference at the White House later that night alongside top administration members, recounting how the shooting unfolded.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

After the shooting, the president reignited calls to build a ballroom at the White House to create a space for safe and secure official events. Trump attended the rescheduled WHCA Dinner that took place in July.

Leavitt’s full interview on the latest "Hang Out with Sean Hannity" will be available Tuesday on YouTube, Spotify and Apple.

World.title: Sylvester Stallone reveals what he said to Trump after surprise Hollywood ambassador appointment
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Sylvester Stallone revealed that he was blindsided when President Donald Trump announced his appointment as a special ambassador to Hollywood.

Days before his second inauguration in January 2025, Trump shared a post on his platform Truth Social in which he named Stallone, Mel Gibson and Jon Voight as "Special Envoys," describing the role as a way for the three actors to serve as his "eyes and ears" in Hollywood and advise him on efforts to bring film and television production back to the U.S.

During a recent interview with The Sunday Times, the 80-year-old "Rocky" star recalled that he found out about the appointment while watching television.

SYLVESTER STALLONE'S 'TULSA KING' SEASON 4 TEASER SPARKS FAN FRENZY: 'THE KING IS BACK!'

"I was watching TV one night, and they go, ‘So Stallone and Mel Gibson and Jon Voight will be …’ And I went, ‘What?’ I said, ‘Excuse me? Really?’ Because if they had asked me in the beginning, I would have said, ‘This is not possible,'" Stallone said.

Stallone told the outlet that he was hesitant about taking on the role because he didn't believe it was feasible. When asked if he had reservations after Trump's announcement, Stallone said, "Yes. Yes, because Hollywood, I guess it’s like feudal states."

'AMERICAN IDOL' DITCHES HOLLYWOOD FOR GEORGIA AFTER TWO DECADES AS CALIFORNIA LOSES ANOTHER PRODUCTION

"They have their little kingdoms," he continued. "You don’t go in and tell six studios how to do things. And Mel Gibson and Jon Voight, we’re kind of do-our-own-thing people. No, it won’t work."

The "Tulsa King" star recalled that he later explained his reasoning to Trump.

"I said thank you and ciao, because it’s impossible," Stallone said. "Hollywood works, and it will evolve."

"It’s corporate, and corporate people won’t want to hear me tell them about finance," he added.

'I PLAY ROCKY' REVIVES THE GAMBLE THAT MADE SYLVESTER STALLONE A SUPERSTAR

In his original post on Jan. 16, 2025, Trump wrote, "It is my honor to announce Jon Voight, Mel Gibson, and Sylvester Stallone, to be Special Ambassadors to a great but very troubled place, Hollywood, California."

"They will serve as Special Envoys to me for the purpose of bringing Hollywood, which has lost much business over the last four years to Foreign Countries, BACK—BIGGER, BETTER, AND STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE!" he continued. "These three very talented people will be my eyes and ears, and I will get done what they suggest. It will again be, like The United States of America itself, The Golden Age of Hollywood!"

DWAYNE 'THE ROCK' JOHNSON REJECTS HOLLYWOOD’S POLITICAL OBSESSION, BLASTS CELEBRITY ATTACK CULTURE

At the time, Gibson, 70, shared that he was caught off-guard by Trump's announcement and did not have previous knowledge about his presidential appointment.

"I got the tweet at the same time as all of you and was just as surprised," he told Variety in January 2025. "Nevertheless, I heed the call. My duty as a citizen is to give any help and insight I can."

"Any chance the position comes with an Ambassador’s residence?" Gibson joked.

Though Stallone may not have been onboard with his role as a special Hollywood ambassador, the action star appears to have a friendly relationship with Trump and heaped praise on the president during a speech following his victory in the November 2024 election.

Days after the election, Stallone introduced Trump at the America First Policy Institute Gala held at the president-elect's Mar-A-Lago Club in Palm Beach, Florida.

"We’re in the presence of a really mythical character," Stallone said of Trump. "I love mythology. And this individual does not exist on this planet. Nobody in the world could have pulled off what he pulled off, so I’m in awe."

"When George Washington defended his country, he had no idea that he was gonna change the world," he added. "Because without him, you could imagine what the world would look like. Guess what? We got the second George Washington."

Stallone was later selected as a 2025 Kennedy Center honoree, with Trump personally naming him among that year’s recipients alongside George Strait, KISS, Gloria Gaynor and Michael Crawford.

The actor has backed Republicans, including John McCain and Trump, but his political history has not been strictly partisan. Over the years, Stallone has made financial contributions to both political parties, donating to various Democratic candidates and committees, including former President Joe Biden and the Democratic National Committee, as well as Republican campaigns.

Meanwhile, Voight, who is a staunch supporter of Trump, appears to have embraced his role as a special ambassador. He has met with the White House and advocated for policies aimed at bringing film and TV production back to the U.S., especially a federal film tax incentive. Voight has been working with his manager Steven Paul and Paul’s associate Scott Karol as part of his push.

After meeting with the trio at the end of last month, Trump threw his support behind a federal film and television production incentive, urging Congress to pass bipartisan legislation to "save" the American entertainment business.

In a Truth Social post on Aug. 31, Trump wrote that "Hollywood is a Complete and Total Disaster" and said there was "no incentive" for productions to stay there. He said meetings were being set up with leaders of both parties and urged Republicans and Democrats to "immediately craft Legislation to save the Movie, Television, and Entertainment Business in America."

Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) and U.S. Representative Laura Friedman (D-CA) later issued statements in which they voiced their support for Trump's proposal.

They’ve been very busy, both of those guys actually have been extremely busy," Voight said.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani on Monday said NYC welcomed all members of the media for a joint meeting with President Donald Trump, who recently banned certain media outlets from the White House.

"I told the president that we're going to have all of the members of the press here on the lawn. And that is something that I believe in, as everyone, no matter the opinion or the critique that we engage in," Mamdani said.

TRUMP, MAMDANI SET TO MEET AGAIN ON MAYOR’S HOME TURF AFTER MONTHS OF POLITICAL WHIPLASH

"I'm only doing it because I think the press also has an obligation," he said.

WHITE HOUSE WON'T BACK DOWN AS ATTORNEY PREDICTS HOW TRUMP'S LATEST PRESS TUSSLE WILL PLAY OUT IN COURT

A Maryland hunter is accused of fatally shooting a woman after mistaking her for a deer while she walked through a Delaware field with her children, according to state police.

Walter Moorhead, 74, was arrested for manslaughter and other charges after he shot Santos Maria Chilel Soto, 39, on Friday evening in Ellendale, Delaware, State Police said in a press release.

Soto was walking through an open field with a man and two children at around 7:40 p.m. as Moorhead was hunting deer from a ground blind, which is a camouflaged structure used by hunters to hide from the sight of game animals.

MANHUNT UNDERWAY IN CALIFORNIA AFTER ARMED SUSPECT ALLEGEDLY POINTS GUN AT PEOPLE, SHOOTS AT OFFICERS

According to police, Moorhead believed he saw a deer and fired his rifle, striking Soto.

State troopers responded to the scene and provided life-saving medical care before Soto was rushed to a local hospital, where she was later pronounced dead.

Moorhead was was slapped with multiple felony charges — manslaughter recklessly causing the death of another person, possession of a firearm during the commission of a felony and three counts of first-degree reckless endangerment.

SUSPECT IN DEATHS OF 5 FOUND DEAD AFTER COPS UNCOVER GRIM SCENE AT RURAL PROPERTY OUTSIDE PORTLAND

He was released from custody after posting a $43,000 cash bond.

The incident remains under investigation.

Soto was described as a mother of five children and a "beloved" aunt, according to a GoFundMe page.

"Maria’s family is now facing the overwhelming pain of this sudden loss while also trying to make sure she is laid to rest with dignity," the fundraiser reads. "This heartbreaking situation has placed a heavy financial burden on the family at a time when they are grieving deeply."

World.title: Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart suffers knee injury against Rams, possible MCL issue feared
World.content:
The optimism and good tidings the New York Giants enjoyed through the first week of the NFL season are suddenly on hold as the team is busy evaluating the status of injured quarterback Jaxson Dart.

Dart, in his second NFL season, injured his left knee during the first series of the Monday Night Football game between the Giants and Los Angeles Rams.

The injury happened on a first-quarter hit when Dart was hit by Rams defenders both high and low. And the low hit seemed to cause his left knee to bend in a manner it is not meant to bend.

That's not all. The team also had a bit of a scare when receiver Malik Nabers left the game after a pass thrown his way fell incomplete. He was seen clutching his right shoulder.

JOHN HARBAUGH AND JAXSON DART AIM TO PULL THE NEW YORK GIANTS OUT OF THE NFC EAST BASEMENT

Nabers returned after missing a couple of series nursing his shoulder on the bench.

The hit on Dart left the quarterback on the ground clutching at the knee of his forward leg when he throws. That is never a good sign.

The saving grace: Dart's leg was not planted on the turf when he was hit.

PATRICK MAHOMES ANSWERS TROUBLING QUESTIONS ABOUT HIS SERIOUS KNEE INJURY ON FIRST DRIVE OF THE CHIEFS SEASON

That allowed the entire part of the lower leg to bend with the knee.

So, this is not a season-ending ACL tear.

MALIK NABERS REVEALS HOW GIANTS COACH JOHN HARBAUGH HELPED HIM OVERCOME HIS ACL INJURY FEARS

But Dart suffered some sort of MCL issue, according to an NFL source. If that is confirmed by an MRI scheduled for Tuesday.

"Yeah, we'll know more tomorrow," coach John Harbaugh said after the game. "That's in the neighborhood of it, I would say. We'll get an MRI tomorrow and have a really good feel for it, and it'll give you more information then."

Dart won't need surgery, but will miss some time. This is not, however, a season-ending injury.

"The fact that it's not that outcome that you're talking about, the devastating outcome, is really good news," Harbaugh said.

Dart limped off the field and was initially treated in the team's medical tent. Several teammates huddled outside the medical tent while Dart was inside, no doubt worried about the status of their starting quarterback.

Backup quarterback Jameis Winston came on in his absence and was largely ineffective, throwing one interception without a touchdown and posting a passer rating of 37.7, which is bad.

World.title: Socialist, communist groups coordinate, promote 'spontaneous' anti-ICE protests in Austin
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Media accounts reported that protesters "quickly organized" a spontaneous anti-ICE protest at an Austin, Texas, intersection following the shooting of a Venezuelan man by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent.

But a Fox News Digital investigation shows that the protests are being promoted and organized by a coordinated network of far-left socialist and communist groups, including the Democratic Socialists of America, the Freedom Road Socialist Organization and the Party for Socialism and Liberation, which works closely with nonprofits funded by Neville Roy Singham, a communist American-born tech tycoon living in Shanghai.

Congressional lawmakers are investigating the Singham network for allegedly fomenting the image of "chaos" in the U.S., including anti-ICE protests from Minneapolis to the Delaney Hall detention center in Newark, N.J. Sure enough, Sunday evening, BreakThrough News, a pro-communist media platform operated by BreakThrough BT Media, a nonprofit funded by Singham, published a "BREAKING NEWS" report from Texas with the headline: "Austin erupts in protest…"

AUSTIN ICE SHOOTING SPARKS FIGHT OVER VENEZUELAN ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT'S DEPORTATION

The shooting occurred Sunday afternoon at about 12:56 p.m. Central Time near Anderson Square and Research Boulevard in Austin. Authorities said an ICE officer shot Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez, a 28-year-old Venezuelan national, during a traffic stop. Perez was hospitalized in serious but stable condition and later placed in federal custody. Local officials said Austin police weren’t involved in the shooting, which is being investigated by federal authorities with assistance from the FBI.

About four hours after the shooting, local socialist and communist activists were already at the scene, waving flags of Mexico, pushing the incident through their national and Texas social-media networks and broadcasting footage of the growing crowd and confrontations with Austin police.

The headlines and descriptions of the demonstration have focused on the protest’s anti-ICE message without identifying the political or ideological infrastructure that helped organize and promote the event. Local media headlines included KVUE reporting that "North Austin ICE shooting draws large protest as tensions escalate," describing a spontaneous outburst: "What began with a handful of people gathered across the street from the scene grew into a much larger crowd over the course of several hours."

But the details of the Austin protest are important because they reveal that the demonstrations represent more than an unplanned gathering of residents responding to a breaking-news event, much like the protests in Minnesota and New Jersey and Minnesota.

SECRET SIGNAL CHATS REVEAL HOW ANTI-ICE AGITATORS COORDINATED NEWARK RIOTS

The shooting provided the immediate trigger, but the mobilization was amplified by organizations with explicit revolutionary socialist and communist ideologies, established propaganda outlets and long-standing ties to international movements aligned with the communist governments of Cuba and Venezuela. They each have pre-existing activist networks and online audiences that organized and promoted the protests.

The event also illustrates how rapidly established activist networks can convert a law-enforcement incident into a larger political action. Within hours, the groups distributed nearly identical claims, promoted the same location and used dramatic language describing the shooting as "ICE terror," "police violence" and part of a pattern of killings.

At about 4:19 p.m. local time, the Party for Socialism and Liberation’s national account, @PSLNational, posted an explosive message on X, announcing the shooting and shouting in capital letters, "BREAKING. MAN SHOT BY ICE AGENTS IN AUSTIN. It called on residents to protest ICE, declaring, "ICE OUT OF AUSTIN NOW!"

Right about then, the group’s Austin chapter shared the dramatic "BREAKING" graphic on Instagram, collaborating with its national headquarters and four Texas chapters in Houston, San Antonio, Dallas-Fort Worth and Waco. By early Monday evening, about 24 hours later, the post had 5,402 likes, 2,016 reposts and 2,391 shares/sends.

DEPROGRAMMED: FORMER DSA INSIDER REVEALS ‘FRIGHTENING’ SOCIALIST AGENDA DROVE HIM FROM ‘EXTREME’ IDEOLOGY

Soon after on Sunday, at about 4:30 p.m. local time, the Austin chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America posted a graphic labeled "Emergency Demonstration/Vigil" calling on supporters to gather at 8121 Research Boulevard from 5 p.m. to 8 p.m. Sunday for a "spontaneous" protest.

"Join us at 8121 Research Blvd from 5-8 p.m. for a spontaneous protest and vigil against yet another instance of ICE and police violence," the post said.

The group later reposted the notice with an updated location and said the demonstration would continue until 7 p.m.

Right about then, the Freedom Road Socialist Organization, an openly Marxist-Leninist group that has sent delegations to support communist regimes in Cuba and Venezuela, and its Austin chapter published its own hyperbolic material about the shooting. One graphic said, "ICE SHOOTS AN UNARMED CIVILIAN," while another described the incident as part of a broader pattern of "ICE violence and killings." Within 24 hours, the post garnered 620 likes, 214 reposts and 156 shares/sends.

The Freedom Road Socialist Organization openly says it is working to build "a new, revolutionary, communist party." In its own program, the group says it wants to replace capitalism through a socialist revolution. The group's program describes the organization as part of the communist movement. In July, the group said it "salutes the Communist Party of China" on the 105th anniversary of its founding.

For years, it’s also supported the Communist Party of Cuba, declaring, "Stand with socialist Cuba," as it praised the Cuban Revolution and called for an end to U.S. sanctions against Cuba.

Videos posted by the group showed demonstrators chanting, holding signs, blocking the roadway near the shooting scene and lighting fireworks.

HASAN PIKER DEFENDS PRO-COMMUNIST, ANTI-ICE SINGHAM NETWORK ACTIVISTS AS 'WONDERFUL PEOPLE'

The Party for Socialism and Liberation official manifesto describes itself as a "revolutionary socialist" movement that "will open the way to communism and the end of class society." The program describes the police and state institutions as tools of capitalist rule and calls for a workers’ government to replace the current system.

The Party for Socialism and Liberation functions as a key boots-on-the-ground mobilizer within the broader activist ecosystem, working alongside Singham-funded organizations such as the People’s Forum, BreakThrough News, CodePink and the ANSWER Coalition on protests, media campaigns and international solidarity efforts.

The Party for Socialism and Liberation also overlaps with the Freedom Road Socialist Organization through shared "anti-imperialist" pro-communist coalitions, while the Democratic Socialists of America often provides a broader layer of street-level organizing and political amplification.

The Party for Socialism and Liberation has participated in international "solidarity" efforts involving Cuba and Venezuela, along with the Freedom Road Socialist Organization, according to a communist publication, Fight Back! News. A self-described communist co-founder of the Party for Socialism and Liberation, Brian Becker, has said the delegation traveled "as comrades in solidarity."

The facts surrounding the shooting remain under investigation. Austin officials have called for transparency and an independent review, while federal authorities have said the ICE agent’s use of force is being investigated. But the protest organizers’ social media posts leave little ambiguity about the political and ideological objective of the protest.

LAWMAKERS THROW OUT 'TROJAN HORSE' ACTIVISTS THEY SAY ARE ENGAGED IN AMERICAN SUBVERSION

At 5:44 p.m., @PSLNational posted a video from the scene, announcing, "LIVE: A crowd has gathered…", and moving from initial messaging to real-time amplification of the street protest. Its national and Austin accounts shared the video on Instagram synchronized with the band Rage Against the Machine’s song, "We’ve Got to Take the Power Back." It added the message, "Austinites flooding the streets where man shot by ICE: ‘ICE out of our neighborhoods,’" giving the illusion of a spontaneous "flooding" of "the streets."

That evening, at 8:27 p.m., @PSLNational published an expanded statement on X, headlined "Justice for Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez," demanding the detainee’s release and the agent's arrest and telling supporters to "follow the example of Minneapolis earlier this year until ICE terror is defeated!"

An identical "Justice for Wilber…" collaborative post on Instagram spread through the Party for Socialism and Liberation’sTexas and national accounts. By early Monday evening, it had 10,600 likes, 3,616 reposts and 2,343 shares/sends.

By about 5 p.m. on Monday, a new call to action moved activists to Pearsal Detention Center, where local groups claimed ICE agents allegedly held the detainee in custody: "WE NEED YOU BOOTS ON THE GROUND…!!!"

World.title: U.S. military leaders divided over action against the Houthis
World.content:
WASHINGTON — U.S. military leaders are divided on whether President Donald Trump should get involved with the conflict between Saudi Arabia and Iranian-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen, according to two U.S. officials.

The Saudis have been asking Trump for the U.S. military to take action against the Houthis, a request that grew more urgent in recent days as the rebels claimed they shot down a Saudi F-15 fighter jet and were quickly advancing on Marib province, which is home to Yemen’s largest oil and gas fields.

Some military leaders are making the case within the Pentagon and to Trump administration officials that opening another military front in the region is a bad idea amid concerns about the Pentagon’s dwindling supply of defensive and long-range weaponry, while noting that the Houthis are not striking U.S. ships, the U.S. officials said.

Yet other military leaders are arguing in favor of strikes, saying the U.S. should help Riyadh retaliate for Houthi strikes in Saudi Arabia and the claim of downing of the F-15 — a challenge to Saudi air superiority over Yemen, the officials said. They said these military leaders are privately expressing concern that for the U.S. not to act more forcefully is a betrayal of an important regional ally.

Trump had ordered strikes against the Houthis to begin around 5 p.m. Eastern Standard Time on Sunday, but the military was notified shortly after 2 p.m. on Sunday that the order was canceled, the two U.S. officials said. One of the officials said Trump has not taken military action off the table in the future.

One senior U.S. military leader in the region specifically warned that action against the Houthis could create unmitigated risk to U.S. troops in Middle East and the Iran war mission, including a U.S. naval blockade and security operations in the Strait of Hormuz, the two U.S. officials said. They said the military leader also made clear that U.S. forces could carry out the Iran mission and strikes against the Houthis and mitigate some of the risks, the officials said.

The internal divide underscores the bind the president is increasingly in as the U.S. remains locked in a war with Iran that he began but has struggled to end, and faces a shortage of key weaponry. The Saudis have been a critical U.S. ally in the Middle East, including throughout the war with Iran. Trump told Fox News over the weekend that he’s deciding whether to escalate the war with Iran, a position he has articulated on and off over the past few months.

The White House and a spokesperson for the Saudi Embassy in Washington, D.C., did not respond to a request for comment. The Pentagon declined to comment.

There has already been tension between the U.S. and its Middle East allies over the war. In May, Saudi Arabia was surprised by an announcement by Trump to help ships through the Strait of Hormuz and suspended the U.S. military’s ability to use its bases and airspace. Trump abruptly reversed his decision.

The U.S. has already been supporting the Saudis by sharing intelligence, helping with planning, sending military advisers forward with the Saudi forces and even providing some logistical support, NBC News has reported. But the Saudis have repeatedly asked the U.S. to do more, including help with strikes against the Houthis.

A satellite view shows the aftermath of the recent drone attack on the East-West pipeline in Saudi Arabia. The attack and the resulting fires, which occurred on Sept. 11, caused significant damage to the pumping station along the pipeline. Vantor

Trump had not shown interest in acting until Thursday, when Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman told him in a phone call that the kingdom cannot succeed alone and after a series of developments — including the Houthis targeting Saudi infrastructure, downing the F-15 and threatening to take control of Yemen’s oil industry, according to one of the U.S. officials.

After the call, Trump ordered the military to provide him with fresh options for strikes against the Houthis, the official said. Chairman of the Joint Chiefs Dan Caine called a 6 p.m. emergency meeting in The Tank, the top-security conference room in the Pentagon, to discuss options, the official said, canceling a trip to Copenhagen to meet with NATO chiefs of defense.

U.S. military officials have presented Trump with options for degrading Houthi military capabilities and stopping the rebels’ recent advances several times since Thursday, the official said, adding that the Pentagon has enough assets in the region to be ready to act if ordered to do so.

Saudi Arabia has closed the East-West pipeline while Houthi fighters captured key locations at the Bab el Mandeb strait Javier Zarracina and Jiachuan Wu / NBC News / ISW; Natural Earth

The New York Times reported some details of Trump’s decision-making process.

Violence escalated over the weekend, as the Houthis said they’d used missiles and drones on Saturday to attack “sensitive” sites in ‌Riyadh and an Aramco facility in the Red Sea city of Yanbu, a key oil export hub.

The spokesperson for the coalition forces issued a statement on Saturday saying Saudi Arabia had successfully intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched toward Riyadh and that the Houthis “target civilians and civilian infrastructure in the capital.”

The militant group also made a rapid advance to control the Bab el Mandeb Strait on the Red Sea, yet another oil chokepoint. The advance has posed a major challenge for the Saudis, who rely on that shipping route particularly since the Strait of Hormuz has been largely shuttered during the Iran war.

The Houthis took control of Yemen in a bloody civil war in 2014 against a Saudi-backed coalition. A fragile truce between the Houthis and the Yemeni government backed by the U.N. was reached in 2022.

Trump announced a ceasefire with the Houthis last year after weeks of punishing strikes against the militant group. Under the deal, the U.S. suspended military action and the Houthis stopped attacking U.S. ships.

Trump recently has said his administration has had discussions with the Houthis but has not offered details. “The Houthis called us, and they don’t want to fight with us,” he said earlier this month. “They would much prefer not having us involved.”

World.title: Appeals court seeks to revive GOP congressional map in Missouri
World.content:
A federal appeals court on Monday introduced a new wrinkle into the convoluted fight over whether Republicans can use a new congressional map in November’s election, as the GOP tries to eliminate one of the state’s two Democratic House districts.

The St. Louis-based 8th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ordered that the new map drawn last year should be used this fall, even though the Supreme Court has already twice rejected Republicans on the issue in recent weeks and had apparently put the issue to bed.

“This Court holds that Missouri’s current plan to use the 2022 map in the November 2026 general election violates the Constitution. Only use of the 2025 map complies with the Constitution and federal law,” the appeals court said in an unsigned ruling.

The decision has no immediate effect and faces long odds to be implemented ahead of the election based on the Supreme Court’s previous action.

The three-judge appeals court panel was comprised of Republican-appointed judges, including two picked by President Donald Trump.

The appeals court put its ruling on hold for a week, giving the challengers time to seek Supreme Court intervention again.

“Ballots have been printed, and Missourians have already voted. Thousands more will vote before this order seeks to take effect. Officials should stop wasting taxpayers’ money on pointless legal action and instead focus on administering our elections,” Richard von Glahn, the executive director of People Not Politicians, the group challenging the map, said in a statement.

Monday’s decision upheld a decision by Missouri-based U.S. District Judge Stephen Clark, who had that the new map must be used, notwithstanding the Missouri Supreme Court having previously reached the opposite conclusion.

The U.S. Supreme Court put Clark’s ruling on hold on Sept. 10 in a decision that seemed to end the dispute, with the state set to use the previous map from 2022, which includes six seats held by Republicans and two held by Democrats. Missouri was one of several states where the Legislature drew a new map last year, seeking to draw out Democratic Rep. Emanuel Cleaver and create a 7-1 GOP map.

Missouri Secretary of State Denny Hoskins, a Republican, had after a significant delay ordered election officials to use the 2022 map.

That followed an unusual proceeding in which the Missouri Supreme Court held him in contempt for failing to comply with its ruling that said the 2025 map had to be put on hold under state law while a voter referendum takes place.

The legal fight began when opponents of the new map gathered sufficient signatures to put the new map before voters in November as a ballot referendum.

But Hoskins delayed a decision about whether to include the measure on the ballot, waiting until the last minute before rejecting the plan, arguing that redistricting plans are not subject to voters’ approval.

World.title: ‘Looksmaxxing’ influencer Clavicular charged with rape in Massachusetts
World.content:
The “looksmaxxing” personality known as Clavicular has been charged with rape in Massachusetts, online court records show.

The charges listed against Clavicular, 20, whose real name is Braden Peters, are one count of rape, one count of drugging someone for sexual intercourse, and one count of procuring liquor for someone under 21 years old, according to the records.

The charges were filed Sept. 8, and the alleged offenses occurred May 23, 2025, the records indicate. More details about the allegations were not immediately available.

Online court records did not show an attorney who could speak on his behalf Monday night.

The Bulwark first reported the charges. A representative for Clavicular, Mitchell Jackson, said the outlet was “exaggerating” in its report and that Clavicular had not been served with an arrest warrant.

“Braden Peters has not been physically served. As usual the Bulwark is exaggerating,” Jackson said in a text message Monday night.

An email to the general mailbox of The Bulwark seeking comment was not immediately returned late Monday.

An arraignment was scheduled for Oct. 14, according to the court records.

Clavicular has gained internet fame — and notoriety — for a trend among young men known as “looksmaxxing,” which Meriam-Webster Dictionary recently called, “The practice of taking one or more sometimes extreme or dangerous measures intended to increase one’s physical attractiveness.”

He has been known for “bone smashing,” or using a hammer to intentionally break facial bones so they grow back stronger or looking better. The trend has been called potentially unhealthy and dangerous by experts.

Clavicular in April was sued by a teenage influencer in Florida who accused him of battery.

Aleksandra Vasilevna Mendoza, who online is known as Alorah or Alorah Ziva, filed a lawsuit in Miami-Dade County that alleged that in 2025 he arranged for her to go to Cape Cod, Massachusetts, gave her vodka until she was drunk, and then had sex with her while she was intoxicated, NBC South Florida reported.

Online court records do not indicate whether the charges of rape, drugging or procurement of alcohol to someone under 21 are related to the allegations in the lawsuit.

Clavicular’s attorney at the time said that he denies the allegations and “intends to vigorously defend himself,” according to the news station.

Clavicular and two other people in April were also charged in Florida with shooting at an alligator. He and another person pleaded no contest to unlawfully discharging a firearm in public and were given six months of probation and ordered to serve 20 hours of community service, according to NBC South Florida.

He was also hospitalized in April in Miami after a suspected overdose. He said in a livestream at the time after being released from the hospital that, “I ain’t gonna be doing any more substances for a little while, hopefully for forever.”

World.title: Drinking finally slows after pandemic spike, but not for every age group
World.content:
Americans are drinking less for the first time since the pandemic, but alcohol use remains higher than it was before 2020, according to a study published Monday in the journal Annals of Internal Medicine.

The decline in drinking rates, though modest at roughly 1%, is welcome news after heavy alcohol use spiked sharply during the pandemic, said senior study author Dr. Brian P. Lee, a liver transplant doctor at Keck Medicine of USC in Los Angeles.

However, Lee said, “these trends haven’t been even across the board.”

While both heavy and occasional drinking declined among Gen Z and millennials from 2022 to 2024, drinking increased in people ages 50 to 64, according to the study, which used data from the National Health Interview Survey conducted by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Lee and his team looked at survey results for four years: 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024.

Overall, men reported a larger decline in drinking than women did from 2022 to 2024 — 2.4% compared with 1.1% — but heavy drinking declined by 9% among women compared with 7.7% among men. The survey defined heavy drinking as either five or more drinks per day or 15 or more per week for men and four drinks per day or eight drinks per week for women.

Gen Z adults reported the biggest decrease in drinking from 2022 to 2024, more than 5%, while millennials reported the largest decline in heavy drinking over the same time period, a drop of 17%. For both age groups, however, the rates of drinking or heavy drinking were still slightly higher than they were in 2018.

Lee said the most concerning finding was that heavy drinking among adults ages 50 to 64 has steadily climbed since 2018. About 2% more people in this age group reported drinking heavily in 2024 compared with 2022, and that number has increased by more than one-third since 2018.

“This 30% increase, that’s about a million people drinking heavily in that age group alone,” Lee said.

Drinking raises a person’s risk of high blood pressure, stroke and digestive problems, and alcohol-related liver disease is now the leading cause of liver transplants in the U.S. Yearly cancer deaths linked to alcohol have doubled over the last three decades.

The older you are, the more vulnerable you are to the damage alcohol can cause, Lee said.

“The average age of developing cirrhosis is in the 50s, and we know someone with a 50-year-old liver is more likely to develop liver scarring with the same quantity of alcohol as a 20-year-old liver,” he said. “The risk with alcohol isn’t the same across all age groups, and this middle-aged group is exactly the group we are worried about.”

People in their 50s and 60s who are currently heavy drinkers have also likely been drinking for years, further exacerbating their risk for alcohol-related health complications, said Dr. Michael Siegel, a professor of public health and community medicine at Tufts University School of Medicine in Boston.

“We’re talking about a substantial amount of alcohol consumption that is probably going to have health effects at that level, and to see that those trends over time have not really decreased is worrisome,” he said.

Alcohol consumption has been steadily on the rise since around the year 2000 after a decline in the late 1980s and ’90s, said Priscilla Martinez-Matyszczyk, deputy scientific director of the Alcohol Research Group, a nonprofit organization. Drinking peaked in 2020, when heavy alcohol use among Americans rose by 20% and any alcohol use rose by 4% compared to 2018.

“We’ve seen this before, where there is a spike in alcohol use after traumatic populationwide events,” Martinez-Matyszczyk said, noting a documented increase in drinking after the 9/11 terrorist attacks. “You’ll see a spike and then a bit of a decline, but often those trends will go back to wherever the trend was heading in the first place, and there was already an increasing trend before the pandemic.”
