World.title: Brugada, Mamdani swap notes on housing, care systems at U20 mayors summit in New York
World.content:
Mexico City’s public care system and Mayor Clara Brugada’s community center initiative won praise from New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani during the 2026 Urban 20 Mayors Summit (U20), an annual gathering of mayors from major G20 cities and other metropolises around the world.

Speaking alongside Brugada in New York on Sunday, Mamdani said that Mexico City is a city “that many of us look to for inspiration, especially in how we answer the crisis of care in our economies.”

Gracias, @NYCMayor, por reconocer las #UTOPÍAS de la Ciudad de México como un proyecto para garantizar una vida plena. Una visión de ciudad que pone a las personas y a las comunidades al centro. ¡Es un gusto que este proyecto sea inspirador en las grandes ciudades del mundo! pic.twitter.com/gvZzhVLnF2 — Clara Brugada Molina (@ClaraBrugadaM) September 20, 2026

“When we’re talking about care blocks, we talk about these often within our own administration as an example of what it can look like to deliver for people in our own city,” he said.

Under Brugada’s leadership, the Mexico City government has set up a public care system, a central part of which is the provision of free childcare as well as services aimed at the well-being of seniors and people with disabilities.

Among the government-run centers that offer these services are Unidades de Transformación y Organización para la Inclusión y la Armonía Social (Units of Transformation and Organization for Inclusion and Social Harmony), known as Utopías. These community centers — which also offer cheap meals and a range of recreational, cultural, social and educational facilities — first opened in Iztapalapa when Bruagada was mayor of that Mexico City borough (2018-23) and are now being expanded to other parts of the capital as the city government seeks to offer greater support to primary caregivers, including working mothers.

Brugada is aiming to open 100 new Utopías during her 2024-30 mayorship, while solidifying caregiving as a “public responsibility” rather than a private one.

Mamdani said that “when we talk about Utopías, [there is] the understanding also that we have to be delivering dignity to working people … to ensure they can live lives that are full, lives that are flourishing.”

“And it is such a pleasure to have a fellow mayor here as we do with the mayors of Freetown and Rome who understand that the issues of the working class must be issues at the forefront of our politics,” he said. “And one day I will return to Mexico City, but I don’t know when that is.”

In separate remarks on Sunday, Mamdani said he would like to work with President Claudia Sheinbaum and “any other leaders from across Mexico” to address “global crises.”

“… The crises we face are global crises and that is true for Mexico City, for Rome, for Freetown, for New York City and so many others. And we’ve also watched in admiration of President Sheinbaum’s initiatives and the ways in which she is tackling the same issues of cost of living,” the mayor said.

Brugada draws inspiration from NYC

While Mamdani looks to Mexico City for inspiration, Brugada was herself inspired by New York, a city she said she visited as a young “social activist” in 1987.

In a social media post, the mayor noted that on Monday, she met with Mamdani and “repartidores paisanos” — i.e. Mexicans who work in the Big Apple as deliverymen and deliverywomen for companies such as Uber Eats and DoorDash.

“In Mexico City we will replicate some of New York’s good practices to support those who work in this activity,” Brugada wrote.

She said her government will create “spaces where [repartidores] can rest, recharge their bikes and access bathrooms.”

“We take care of our workers here and there!” Brugada wrote.

En #NuevaYork me reuní con el alcalde @NYCMayor y con repartidores paisanos. Replicaremos en la Ciudad de México algunas de las buenas prácticas de Nueva York para apoyar a quienes se dedican a esta actividad. Como espacios donde puedan descansar, recargar sus bicis y acceso a… pic.twitter.com/NBd5HeccBm — Clara Brugada Molina (@ClaraBrugadaM) September 21, 2026

On Monday morning, the mayor used the New York City Subway to get to her meeting with Mamdani.

“Hello. We’re going on the subway to City Hall where the Mayor Mamdani awaits us,” she said in a video message.

Above the video, Brugada wrote: “On the way to a meeting with the Mayor of New York. We’re continuing the exchange of ideas and experiences about the future of our cities. As in our beloved #CapitalDeLaTransformación [i.e. Mexico City] public transport is what connects and integrates major metropolises … and here we go.”

Brugada: ‘No (affordable) housing, no peace’

During an address at a U20 forum on affordable housing on Sunday, Brugada said that Mexico City would, “of course,” join a global “affordable housing coalition” proposed by Barcelona Mayor Jaume Collboni.

“I know that many cities present here will [also] join,” she said.

In a video posted to social media, Brugada said that Collboni had made a “very good proposal to build a coalition of cities in favor of affordable housing.”

In the same video, the mayor of Barcelona — a city with serious tourism-related housing problems — said that Mexico City is among the first cities to join “the defense of a fundamental right, as is the right to decent and affordable housing for everyone.”

“This is a fight that all the big cities of the world are in, and I’m very happy that Mexico City together with New York and Toronto … have joined the initiative in order to do big things,” Collboni said.

In her forum address on Sunday, Brugada declared that without affordable housing, there is “no peace,” and spoke about her government’s housing initiatives and the progress made during her mayorship and that of Sheinbaum, who governed Mexico City from December 2018 to June 2023.

“Between 2018 and 2025, nearly half a million people were lifted out of housing poverty in Mexico City. Despite these results, significant challenges remain. As in other cities around the world, the city continues to face a housing shortage, as well as gentrification and the displacement of communities due to speculative dynamics in the real estate market,” she said.

“To address this situation, in Mexico City we have developed the largest housing policy in our history — and one of the policies of greatest reach at an international level as well,” Brugada said.

“The three pillars of this housing policy are firstly, the large-scale construction of social housing; secondly, regulation of the real estate market; and thirdly, we carry this out in partnership with the people through a model of co-management,” she said.

“… We have the goal of building 200,000 … [affordable] homes by 2030,” the mayor said.

“I’m talking about new homes and improved homes. … This means unprecedented progress in reducing the housing shortage,” Brugada said.

Mexico News Daily

World.title: Mass nesting event brings more than 100,000 olive ridley sea turtles to Oaxaca’s Playa Escobilla
World.content:
More than 100,000 olive ridley sea turtles came ashore at Oaxaca’s Playa Escobilla in a single mass nesting event last week, but the spectacle masks a fragile reproductive outlook: As few as 30% to 40% of the eggs may hatch.

According to the newspaper El Universal Oaxaca, 101,500 females emerged from the Pacific Ocean in Santa María Tonameca last Tuesday in a huge, synchronous nesting event known as an arribada.

The sixth arribada (literally “arrival” in Spanish) of the 2026-27 season lifted the season’s running total to more than 465,000 turtles as of last week, according to the paper.

The olive ridley turtle is among the smallest species of sea turtle in the world. They are found primarily in tropical regions, with a nesting season that generally runs from May through February or March.

Playa Escobilla is among the world’s leading nesting sites for the olive ridley, or Lepidochelys olivacea.

The species is listed as endangered in Mexico and faces risks from egg poaching, fishing, destruction of nesting habitat and climate-related events. Conservation efforts are abundant all over Mexico, and volunteer opportunities are many, as detailed this month in Mexico News Daily.

Despite the current large Escobilla tally, Rafael Villanueva Alcázar of the National Commission of Natural Protected Areas (Conanp) cautions that nesting totals do not guarantee a comparable increase in hatchlings.

“It sounds like a lot,” he said, “but it’s actually very low compared to other beaches that have a higher rate of hatchling production.”

Only about 30% to 40% of Escobilla nests hatch, Villanueva said. By comparison, Playa Ceuta in Sinaloa estimates an 85% hatch rate, but it has only about 500 olive ridley nests per season.

No global hatching rate for sea turtle nests could be found, but one widely cited statistic is that roughly one in every 1,000 sea turtle hatchlings worldwide survives to adulthood.

Rising sand temperatures, changes in sand composition, erosion, strong swells and low humidity are among the factors reducing hatching success. Egg theft and other human-caused damage also take a toll.

Conditions can vary sharply between seasons and sanctuaries.

At Morro Ayuta, another major olive ridley refuge on Oaxaca’s coast, a record 1.9 million olive ridley nests were protected and more than 34 million hatchlings were released into the sea during the 2025-26 season.

Guillermo González Padilla, the head of that turtle camp, said those numbers were “unprecedented” thanks to “the rains, the wetter beaches and the fact that the summer’s temperature [in 2025] was ideal for egg incubation.”

(For this season, Morro Ayuta had counted about 135,000 turtles through the start of its third arribada earlier this month, according to Conanp.)

Meanwhile, at Escobilla, conservation work over the past 35 years has helped. Officials set aside a 5-kilometer protected area for nesting during last week’s arribada, and Conanp is monitoring the nesting grounds along with other federal agencies and local communities.

Local participation is critical because available park rangers alone cannot protect the beach from poachers and other threats. Also, according to EDUCA, a Oaxacan community development NGO, locals help strategically relocate eggs — which average 100 per nest — after arribadas.

With reports from El Universal Oaxaca and MeganoticiasMx

World.title: Aeroméxico investigates possible leak of 15 million passenger records
World.content:
Aeroméxico is investigating a possible leak of customer information after the federal Ministry of Anti-Corruption and Good Governance (SABG) identified an online user offering to sell a trove of over 15 million passenger records.

However, Aeroméxico said Sunday that it hadn’t identified any compromise of its customers’ financial information.

🚨Detectan posible exposición de datos personales vinculada a Aeroméxico La Secretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno identificó indicios de una posible filtración de datos personales en un sistema que podría estar relacionado con Aeroméxico. El hallazgo surgió tras detectar,… pic.twitter.com/iSFbFpKhkx — Azucena Uresti (@azucenau) September 20, 2026

In a statement, Aeroméxico said that “based on the information available,” it hadn’t identified any “exposure” of its customers’ “financial information,” including details of cards used to purchase flights.

The airline also said it hadn’t detected any compromise of customers’ Aeroméxico account passwords, including those used to access the Aeroméxico rewards program.

“Furthermore, this situation has not created any impact on our operations,” Aeroméxico said.

The airline released its statement after SABG said it had detected that a user of the social media and instant messaging platform Telegram was attempting to sell a 1.1 gigabyte database “supposedly attributable” to Aeroméxico and containing more than 15 million passenger records.

“Within the framework of active forensic monitoring of possible security incidents, the Ministry of Anti-Corruption and Good Governance identified signs of a possible exposure of personal data in a system that could be related to Aeroméxico,” the SABG said in a statement.

The ministry said that its monitoring allowed it to locate a Sept. 18 post on Telegram in which “a user offers a database supposedly attributable to Aeroméxico with more than 15 million records,” including — allegedly — the full names of customers of the airline, their e-mail addresses, their telephone numbers and their dates of birth.

The SABG said that it “obtained a sample of 100,092 records” and subsequently identified the names of various people, including those of public servants and public figures.

The ministry said it would “analyze the data obtained” and begin an investigation aimed at determining “the alleged responsibility for the compromised databases.”

Aeroméxico said it would cooperate with federal authorities and report on any relevant developments in a timely manner.

The airline also said it had begun its own “exhaustive investigation” in order to “verify the authenticity and veracity” of the information being offered to “third parties,” determine “its origin” and “establish the reach of any possible impact.”

While the airline said it hadn’t identified any compromise of its customers’ financial information, it advised its customers to stay alert to “unusual e-mails, messages or calls that seek personal or financial information.”

Aeroméxico didn’t say that its systems or databases had been targeted in a cyberattack.

However, hackers have previously targeted both companies and federal and state governments in Mexico. Among the victims of previous cyberattacks are the Ministry of National Defense and state oil company Pemex.

Mexico News Daily

World.title: Sheinbaum pledges continued military support as Sinaloa’s cartel turf war shifts to Mazatlán
World.content:
A day after pledging Sunday to keep federal security forces in Sinaloa “as long as necessary,” President Sheinbaum on Monday repeated her conviction that U.S. interference precipitated the cartel turf war plaguing the troubled state. The violence, previously centered in Culiacán and rural areas, has spread south in recent months to the resort city of Mazatlán.

While in Culiacán, the Sinaloa state capital, on Sunday, Sheinbaum said Governor Graciela Domínguez can count on the complete support of the federal government.

Domínguez has been in office for less than a month after being appointed on Aug. 25 to replace Rubén Rocha, who was indicted by U.S. federal prosecutors for alleged links to drug trafficking.

“First and foremost, all federal forces … will remain here for as long as necessary,” she said. “We will not withdraw any element of the Army, the National Guard or the Navy; they will continue to support the governor and, above all, the people of Sinaloa.”

The state has been embroiled in a civil war between factions of the Sinaloa Cartel for two years, becoming what El País newspaper has described as “the biggest political crisis of Sheinbaum’s term.”

As the turf war spread to Mazatlán this summer, the government has deployed thousands of federal troops to the resort city, including 1,000 marines and over 800 Public Security Ministry agents last week. Despite an increase in military presence, homicides in Mazatlán outpaced killings in the larger city of Culiacán in August.

Sinaloa’s economy is facing a historic downturn, driven by severe security challenges and cartel-related violence, leading to a contraction of 4.5% in this year’s first quarter.

On Sunday, Sheinbaum blamed foreign interference for the current situation and then doubled down on that claim during her daily press conference on Monday.

“We don’t want interference from any foreign government in our territory,” she said on Sunday. “Interference generates violence, whereas cooperation for development generates peace.”

Sheinbaum said that before the U.S. “extraction” of drug kingpin Ismael Zambada, the murder rate in Sinaloa was low (“less than one homicide per day,” she claimed). Since then, violence has escalated, producing significant crime rates.

Sunday’s visit was Sheinbaum’s first to the state since the indictments against Rocha and nine other government and law enforcement officials from the state were made public in April.

To address the challenges, Sheinbaum said federal officials would travel in stages to Sinaloa; Security Cabinet officials will visit this week, followed by officials from the Agriculture Ministry.

“There will be no shortage of money to support farmers,” she said, acknowledging that agriculture is the backbone of the state’s economy.

With reports from N+, La Jornada and El País

World.title: After a shootout, authorities rescue 3 kidnapping victims and arrest 7 suspects in Puerto Peñasco
World.content:
Security forces arrested seven people and freed three kidnapping victims during an operation Friday afternoon in Puerto Peñasco, Sonora, a popular seaside resort city also known as Rocky Point.

Authorities also seized an arsenal that included more than 40 long guns, approximately 4,000 rounds of ammunition, two Minimi machine guns and a Browning M2 .50 caliber gun, the federal Security Cabinet announced on Monday.

En Puerto Peñasco, Sonora, trabajos de investigación de @fgjesonora, con información del Centro Nacional de Inteligencia de @SSPCMexico @Defensamx1, @SEMAR_mx y @Amicsonora.

En una operación encabezada por @Defensamx1 y @Amicsonora permitieron ubicar un inmueble relacionado con… pic.twitter.com/dtwS2fGtft — Omar H Garcia Harfuch (@OHarfuch) September 21, 2026

Security Minister Omar García Harfuch said that three federal agencies and the military joined an investigation by the Sonora Attorney General’s Office (FGJES), supplying intelligence that allowed state officials to identify a property linked to the kidnappings.

As state police and soldiers approached the premises, armed civilians opened fire. The authorities returned fire, eventually outflanking the suspects and containing them.

Three Sonora Investigative Police agents were wounded in the confrontation, none seriously, and three kidnapping victims were freed. Authorities captured seven suspects, including one minor.

The suspects will face charges for attempted aggravated homicide, crimes against public servants, aggravated vehicle theft, criminal association and kidnapping.

After the shootout, the authorities obtained a search warrant and re-entered the property, confiscating the weapons. The search also turned up evidence that was sufficient to merit another warrant that led to two weekend raids on additional properties in downtown Puerto Peñasco.

The sweep of those locations resulted in the seizure of heroin, methamphetamine, loaded magazines, bullet-proof vests, tactical gear and three high-end vehicles which had been reported stolen in the United States.

“We extend special recognition to the three AMIC [the Criminal Investigation Agency] agents who were injured during the attack,” García Harfuch said in a social media post.

A FGJES press release indicated that one of its agents was shot in a lower extremity, while two female agents suffered shrapnel wounds. All three were reported to be in stable condition.

The skirmish came about after several miners reported to police that they had escaped a kidnapping attempt last week, but others hadn’t. State officials alerted federal agencies, who were able to follow the route of the captors and locate a white Chevrolet Suburban truck that had been described by the near-victims.

With reports from La Jornada, Sonora Presente and Eje Central

World.title: Hurricane Polo expected to reach Category 5 as it nears Mexico’s Pacific coast
World.content:
Listen to this article

Hurricane Polo is expected to quickly intensify after forming Monday morning in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Guerrero, with Civil Protection encouraging residents of several states to remain vigilant and follow safety recommendations.

Polo could bring heavy rain, rough surf and tropical-storm-force winds to parts of Mexico this week as it intensifies into a Category 5 hurricane near the coast of Michoacán by Wednesday, the U.S. National Hurricane Center warned.

⚠️ #Polo ahora como #Huracán categoría 1 ⚠️ ◾️Se localiza a 305 km al sur-suroeste de Zihuatanejo, #Guerrero, y a 435 km al sur-sureste de Manzanillo, #Colima

◾️Su circulación refuerza la psibabilidad de #Lluvias de distintas intensidades en Jalisco, Colima, Michoacán, Guerrero… pic.twitter.com/3RRiy2j0PQ — Coordinación Nacional de Protección Civil (@CNPC_MX) September 21, 2026

It was centered about 410 kilometers south-southeast of Manzanillo, Mexico, and 322 kilometers southwest of Zihuatanejo at 9 a.m. CST on Monday. As of 12 p.m., it was a Category 1 storm with maximum sustained winds of 129 kph (80 mph).

Mexico’s National Meteorological Service (SMN) predicted Monday that Polo would bring heavy rainfall to Pacific coastal regions, potentially raising river and stream levels, triggering flooding and mudslides.

Intense rain is expected over the coming days in the states of Oaxaca and Guerrero (75 to 150 millimeters), very heavy rainfall (50 to 75 mm) in Michoacán, and heavy rainfall (25 to 50 mm) in coastal Jalisco and Colima.

Winds of 10 to 20 kph, with gusts of 30 to 50 kph, can also be expected along the coasts of Colima, Michoacán, Guerrero and Oaxaca. In addition, the storm will bring waves of 1 to 3 meters to Guerrero, Michoacán, Oaxaca, Jalisco and Colima.

Officials urged the public to remain attentive to the warnings issued by Mexico’s National Meteorological Service (SMN) and to follow the recommendations of Civil Protection.

The SMN and the U.S. National Hurricane Center established a watch zone from Tecpan de Galeana, Guerrero, to Punta San Telmo, Michoacán, warning that Polo’s trajectory will be “erratic.” It is expected to curve and move parallel to the coasts of Colima, Michoacán and Guerrero.

Farther west in the Pacific Ocean, Tropical Storm Odalys is forecast to become a hurricane by mid-week. It was located over 2,000 kilometers west-southwest of the southern tip of Mexico’s Baja California peninsula on Monday morning.

In September 2024, Hurricane John hit coastal Guerrero as a Category 3 storm, just one year after Category 5 Hurricane Otis devastated Acapulco, one of Mexico’s main tourist destinations with a population of over one million people, from which it is still recovering.

With reports from AP News

World.title: MND Local Guadalajara: Airport road update and Line 5’s environmental cost
World.content:
This week, we have an update on construction of the Guadalajara International Airport’s second entrance and how the buildout of bus rapid transit (Line 5) along the Chapala highway has affected the local environment.

Airport’s 2nd entrance road now expected to open by March 2027

The project to add a second airport entrance kicked off in earnest 13 months ago. It aimed to ease chronic traffic bottlenecks along the Chapala highway, where airport travelers, daily commuters and commercial trucks all battle for scarce road space.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Gobierno de Jalisco (@gobjalisco)

In summer 2025, public officials promised the work would be finished in time for the FIFA World Cup earlier this summer, but that deadline came and went. Then work was suspended to prevent construction delays around the airport during the tournament.

Now that work has resumed, we have an updated timeline for completion. Earlier this month, Jalisco Gov. Pablo Lemus Navarro declared the airport’s new 6-kilometer entrance road should be ready for its debut by March 2027.

“The Guadalajara Airport will have a second entrance; it will no longer only be possible to enter via the Chapala Highway,” he told local newspaper El Informador. “This is good news for connectivity and mobility from the airport.”

The new road will connect Adolf Horn Avenue with the airport’s south side. For southbound drivers coming from areas like Tlajomulco, Tlaquepaque and Zapopan, the road will allow them to bypass the initial segment of the Chapala highway. It will also alleviate northbound traffic congestion on the Chapala highway by diverting drivers to Adolfo Horn.

Additional airport upgrades

In addition to a second airport access road, the project includes an internal interchange and new roads to connect to the airport’s future Terminal 2.

But that is not all. The final phase of work to modernize the Chapala highway also got started this month. This project involves new pedestrian bridges, public transport stations, storm drainage, sidewalks, streetlights, bike lanes and replacement trees (more on that below).

These improvements are expected to take eight months to complete, with final delivery by May 2027.

Airport access improvements are being jointly funded by the Jalisco state government and airport operator Pacific Airport Group (GAP). Guadalajara International Airport is the third busiest in Mexico, with annual passenger traffic of nearly 18.8 million in 2025.

The high environmental cost of the city’s new Line 5 mass transit system

The extension of public transit to the Guadalajara airport was constructed in a rush ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. This new link to Guadalajara’s mass transit system was dubbed Line 5, even though it’s not a light rail system like Lines 1 through 4.

The impetus behind the new Line 5 was not visionary public planning but a FIFA requirement for all host cities, which mandated that tournament visitors have a public transport option from the airport to the soccer stadium. Chronic traffic bottlenecks along the Chapala highway, the sole access point to Guadalajara airport, also threatened to embarrass public officials on the world stage, something they were desperate to avoid.

Line 5 was completed in time for June’s World Cup matches. While some lamented the lack of rail service on this congested route, the project was widely hailed as a success.

The part that’s received far less attention is the environmental cost of this new infrastructure. Below is a look at that scorecard.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Pablo Lemus Navarro (@pablolemusn)

Constructing six new BRT stations over a 22.5-kilometer stretch of the Chapala highway involved the elimination of 1,541 trees along the route, according to the Ministry of Environment and Territorial Development.

All the trees cut were located in the El Salto and Tlajomulco municipalities, with authorization granted by local officials.

Tree cover loss and its effects

An environmental impact assessment completed ahead of Line 5’s construction identified 32 tree species (97% of which were deemed healthy), 133 bird species and six reptile species inhabiting the wooded areas in its path. The trees were removed anyway, with subsequent plans to add 2,846 new trees.

How has the sudden removal of so much tree cover impacted the urban area?

Dr. Lucila Méndez Morán of the Department of Applied Ecology at Centro Universitario de Ciencias Biológicas y Agropecuarias (CUCBA) explained that deforestation on the city’s south side tied to Line 5 has intensified the “urban heat island” effect already afflicting this part of the metropolitan area.

The loss of vegetation and shade not only elevates local temperatures but also reduces the area’s ability to absorb water during the rainy season, dampen noise and flush air pollutants. The state has said that while the short-term environmental impact of Line 5 is negative, the landscape should improve over the medium term.

Despite more trees being replanted than removed, it’s not a net benefit, ecologically speaking. The amount of oxygen generated by small tree saplings is a fraction of what’s generated by mature trees. Until those trees grow to maturity over the coming decade or more, their loss will be acutely felt.

Line 5 construction compounds legacy environmental issues

Massive tree loss in Tlajomulco and El Salto is especially painful due to a well-documented environmental crisis that predates the construction of Line 5.

Uncontrolled real estate expansion on the city’s south side in recent decades has already stripped much of the forest cover, raising local temperatures by 2 degrees to 3 degrees Celsius relative to other parts of the Guadalajara Metropolitan Area (GMA). Besides Tlajomulco and El Salto, this area also includes popular tourist destinations Tlaquepaque and Tonalá.

In addition, this zone suffers severe air pollution tied to chronic heavy traffic, under-regulated industrial emissions and thermal inversions in wintertime.

Going forward, this poses a risk of worse public health outcomes due to poor air quality and even hotter temperatures.

MND writer Dawn Stoner is reporting from Guadalajara.

What to See & Do

TUESDAY IN SÃO PAULO

TODAY’S PICK — FREE ART ON PAULISTA MASP until 8 pm, then Japan House Start at MASP on Avenida Paulista, free all Tuesday. It stays open until 8 pm, rare for a weekday, so you can linger. The famous glass easels hold European classics, while the basement café is pricey but calm. Then walk about 20 minutes (or ride one stop on Line 2 Green to Brigadeiro) to Japan House São Paulo on the same avenue, free and open until 6 pm. Its current design shows rotate often, so check the ground-floor screens for what is on. Both are indoors and air-conditioned, ideal if the afternoon turns humid. Take Line 2 Green to Trianon-Masp, single fare R$5.40. For a gentle finish, Sesc Paulista, a short walk from Japan House at Avenida Paulista 119, has a public terrace café worth a look.

OUTDOORS — LAKE LOOP AT IBIRAPUERA A late-afternoon walk before sunset Parque Ibirapuera opens daily from 5 am to midnight and stays free. Arrive around 4:30 pm via the Line 5 Lilac AACD-Servidor station, then walk the lake loop. The sunset is near 6:04 pm, and the light over the far side of the lake is best just before then. Rent a bike near Gate 3 or simply walk; there are water fountains and shaded benches every few hundred metres.

COFFEE & WHERE TO WORK — PINHEIROS Reliable wifi and a quiet table Head to Coffee Lab on Rua Fradique Coutinho in Pinheiros. It opens early, has strong wifi, and serves a serious flat white. Expect to pay around R$18 to R$26 for a drink with a snack. For a coworking desk, WeWork Paulista has day passes, but book before you go. Alternatively, the Café Girondino in Centro has a lovely historic room, though it gets busier by midday.

THE CONTRASTING PLAY — CENTRO’S NOISE Mercadão and Farol Santander For the opposite mood, go to Mercado Municipal, free entry, open 6 am to 6 pm. The stained-glass windows and mezzanine fruit stalls feel like old São Paulo. Then walk eight minutes to Farol Santander, open 9 am to 8 pm, R$45. The viewing deck offers a dense Central skyline. This is a busier, louder option than Paulista, best reached by Line 1 Blue to São Bento.

TONIGHT, AFTER 7 PM A jazz-leaning or gallery-night route MASP remains the anchor: it closes at 8 pm, so an after-dinner visit works. The area around Rua dos Pinheiros has relaxed wine bars open late on Tuesday. For music, check Casa de Francisca in Centro (Rua Quintino Bocaiúva, Sé), which runs intimate acoustic shows, usually ticketed around R$70. Booking is wise. If you prefer open air, the terraces at Praça Benedito Calixto are quieter on a Tuesday evening than at the Saturday fair.

ALSO ON TODAY Museu da Língua Portuguesa — Centro — 9 am–4:30 pm, R$25, free Tuesday MAC USP — Ibirapuera — 10 am–9 pm, free Museu do Ipiranga — Ipiranga — 10 am–5 pm, R$30 Sesc Pompeia — Pompeia — 10 am–8 pm, free Beco do Batman — Vila Madalena — open-air, always open, free Sala São Paulo guided visit — Luz/Campos Elíseos — free visits, concerts ticketed

04

Getting Around

TRANSPORT

Single metro fare is R$5.40 across Lines 1 Blue, 2 Green, 3 Red, 4 Yellow and 5 Lilac; CPTM trains use the same integrated fare with a Bilhete Único.

Today’s rodízio, Tuesday 22, restricts plates ending 3 and 4 in the expanded centre from 7 am to 10 am and 5 pm to 8 pm. Use the metro during those windows if your plate ends in 3 or 4.

05

Where to Eat

LUNCH & DINNER

Lunch: Mocotó Café inside the Mercado de Pinheiros food market, Rua Pedro Cristi 89, Pinheiros. It is open on Tuesdays until 5 pm.

It serves a short menu of north-eastern Brazilian classics. Try baião de dois, rice and beans cooked together, or dadinhos de tapioca, crisp tapioca and cheese cubes.

Dinner: A Casa do Porco, a pork-focused restaurant at Rua Araújo 124 in República, near the city centre. Michelin lists it as a good-value Bib Gourmand pick.

It opens at noon on Tuesdays and takes walk-ins. Leave your name with the host and you get a waiting time. Tuesday to Thursday, 3 pm to 6:30 pm is quietest.

Worth the trip: the original Mocotó, Avenida Nossa Senhora do Loreto 1100, Vila Medeiros, in the north zone. It opens at noon and takes reservations online.

06

Practical Info

GOOD TO KNOW

Driving: today’s rodízio, the city’s weekday car ban, applies to plates ending in 3 and 4. It runs 7–10 am and 5–8 pm in the expanded centre.

Paying for transport: the single metro fare is R$5.40. CPTM commuter trains take tap-to-pay bank cards at all turnstiles.

The metro began adding tap-to-pay gates on 14 September and expects to finish in October. If a gate will not read your card, use a Bilhete Único transit card.

Emergency numbers: dial 190 for the Military Police, 192 for SAMU, the public ambulance service, and 193 for the fire brigade.

Light and weather: sunset is at 6:04 pm. The day stays warm and mostly dry, but carry a small umbrella for a passing shower.

07

Community & Lifestyle

FOR NEWCOMERS

Museum week: the 20th Primavera dos Museus, a national festival run by the federal museums institute Ibram, lasts until Sunday 27 September.

This year’s theme is ‘Museums for All People’. Many São Paulo museums add free talks, games and tours, so check your nearest museum’s social media.

Science park: the museums of Instituto Butantan, the state vaccine and research centre, join in from Wednesday. A family discovery game starts at 11:30 am, with no sign-up.

On Saturday at 9 am, its public health museum leads a walk through Bom Retiro and Luz. Meet at Luz station, by the exits facing Jardim da Luz park; sign up on WhatsApp at (11) 93448-5845.

Paperwork: on a temporary visa, you must register with the Federal Police within 90 days of arrival. With a residence permit, you have 30 days from its official publication.

Election day: Brazil holds its general election on Sunday 4 October, with voting from 8 am to 5 pm. Foreign residents cannot register to vote.

08

Game Day

FOOTBALL

There is no official match this week for Palmeiras, Corinthians, São Paulo or Santos. The Brasileirão, Brazil’s national league, is paused for the international window.

The first big game back in the city is São Paulo v Santos on Friday 2 October at 8 pm. It is played at Morumbis, São Paulo FC’s stadium, and was postponed from July.

The league then resumes on 7–8 October. Palmeiras host Bahia on Thursday 8 October at 9:30 pm at Nubank Parque, their stadium.

The Dérbi, the Palmeiras v Corinthians rivalry match, follows on Sunday 11 October at 5:30 pm, also at Nubank Parque.

Palmeiras are also in the semifinals of the Copa Libertadores, South America’s top club competition. They got through 4–3 on penalties after a 3–3 aggregate draw. They face Fluminense of Rio over two legs, on 14 and 21 October.

09

Business & Markets

WEEK IN FIGURES

The Ibovespa, the main index of Brazil’s stock exchange in São Paulo, rose 0.74% on Monday to close at 186,595.60 points.

The Brazilian real gained 0.61% against the US dollar, ending at R$5.1095 per dollar. A stronger real makes imported goods and trips abroad a little cheaper.

Wall Street also had a strong day. The S&P 500 rose 1.49% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq gained 2.26%.

At 8 am today, the Central Bank publishes the minutes of its Copom meeting. Copom is the committee that sets the Selic, Brazil’s benchmark interest rate.

On 16 September it cut the Selic from 14% to 13.75%, the fifth cut in a row, in a unanimous vote. The minutes explain why, and hint at what could come next.

For newcomers, the Selic shapes what banks charge for loans and pay on savings. Lower rates usually mean cheaper credit, but the change reaches customers slowly.

10

Plan Ahead

THE WEEK

THE DAYS AHEAD TUE 22 — Blue Note São Paulo, in the Conjunto Nacional building at Avenida Paulista 2073, hosts a Miles Davis tribute at 8 pm WED 23 — Sunniest day of the week; Instituto Butantan’s museum discovery game starts at 11:30 am, no sign-up needed SAT 26 — Guided walk through Bom Retiro and Luz at 9 am, from Luz station; sign up by WhatsApp first SUN 27 — Last day of the Primavera dos Museus festival, with extra activities in museums across the city FRI 2 OCT — São Paulo v Santos at Morumbis, 8 pm, the first local league game after the break SUN 4 OCT — General election, first round; voting runs 8 am–5 pm. The 50th São Paulo International Film Festival follows, 15–29 October

Background: São Paulo Nightlife Tonight: Terra Tremesse, Twelve Metres Down.

Background: São Paulo Daily Brief — Monday, September 21, 2026.

11

FAQ

QUICK ANSWERS

Which car plates are banned from driving in central São Paulo today?

Today, Tuesday, the rodízio car ban covers plates ending in 3 and 4. It applies in the expanded centre from 7 am to 10 am and from 5 pm to 8 pm. If your plate ends in 3 or 4, take the metro in those hours. A single fare costs R$5.40.

Is MASP free to visit today?

Yes. MASP, the São Paulo Museum of Art on Avenida Paulista, is free on Tuesdays and open from 10 am to 8 pm. Japan House São Paulo, on the same avenue, is open today from 10 am to 6 pm. It is closed on Mondays.

Can I watch a São Paulo club play this week?

No. The Brasileirão, Brazil’s national league, is paused for the international window, so Palmeiras, Corinthians, São Paulo and Santos have no official games. The first local game is São Paulo v Santos at Morumbis on Friday 2 October at 8 pm. The league resumes on 7–8 October.

What are the Copom minutes published today?

They are the Central Bank’s written record of its 16 September meeting, published at 8 am Brasília time. That meeting cut the Selic interest rate to 13.75%. The minutes explain the reasons for the cut. Markets read them for hints about future rates, which affect loans and savings.

I have just moved to Brazil. When must I register with the Federal Police?

On a temporary visa, you must register within 90 days of arriving in Brazil. With a residence permit, you have 30 days from its official publication. Registration gives you the RNM, your national migration number and ID card. Late registration can lead to a fine.

World.title: Rio de Janeiro Daily Brief — Tuesday, September 22, 2026
World.content:
Rio de Janeiro — A warm, partly cloudy Tuesday is set for Rio, with only light rain risk — ideal for a museum morning and a beach check later.

The headline story is calm: no major match or festival, so the pick is a low-key culture day in Centro and the port zone.

Market mood was risk-on stateside, with tech leading the advance as Treasury yields eased back from the 5% threshold.

In one line: use a quiet Tuesday for reopened museums, a long lunch, and an early beach walk before sunset.

Rio de Janeiro Daily Brief for Tuesday, September 22, 2026. Photo: The Rio Times archive.

Weather & What to Wear

FOUR-DAY OUTLOOK

WED 23 27°C 30% rain THU 24 26°C 40% rain FRI 25 25°C 55% rain SAT 26 24°C 60% rain

Today feels warm and slightly humid, with scattered cloud building through the afternoon. A thin rain chance sits near 20 to 30 percent, mostly after 3pm.

Wear light clothing, carry a small umbrella, and plan outdoor time for the morning or early afternoon. Evenings stay mild near 21°C.

From Thursday onward the rain risk climbs toward 55–60 percent, so treat today and Wednesday as the dry window for longer walks.

Sunset today: 5:49 pm · Water near 23°C with waist-high waves and moderate rips; most posts flying yellow caution flags.

Day at a Glance

SNAPSHOT

03

What to See & Do

TUESDAY IN RIO

TODAY’S PICK — PORT ZONE & CENTRO CULTURE Museu do Amanhã and free art, with a seafood lunch Start at the Museu do Amanhã in Praça Mauá, open today from 10am to 6pm. Entry is R$30, or R$15 for half-price — the science and climate exhibits suit a digital-nomad audience. Take the VLT to Parada dos Museus from Centro or the ferry side if you are near Praça XV. Afterward walk across Praça Mauá to the Museu de Arte do Rio (MAR), open Thursday to Tuesday from 11am to 6pm. Entry is R$20, but Tuesday is free — today you save the ticket. Go for the rooftop terrace and the African-Brazilian collection. Spend two to three hours in the port zone, then a 15-minute VLT ride returns you to Carioca or Cinelândia. The area is safe in daylight and busy around the museums.

OUTDOORS — GARDEN MORNING Botanical garden calm before the rain The Jardim Botânico opens today from 8am to 5pm (on Wednesdays from 11am). Foreigners pay R$80, Brazil residents R$40 — carry proof of residence for the lower rate. The imperial palm avenue is at its best in the morning light. Walk the orchid house and the sensory garden before the heat builds. It is a good place for a long call-free stroll and drains crowds midweek. From the garden, Aterro do Flamengo is a short taxi away if you want a sea-front finish before the late rain risk.

COFFEE & WHERE TO WORK — CENTRO & IPANEMA Strong internet and good tables Curto Café in Centro, near Rua da Assembleia, does specialty espresso and decent wifi until early evening on weekdays. Tables by the window work well for a laptop hour after the museum. In Ipanema, Co.W. Coworking at Farme de Amoedo offers day passes around R$60 to R$90, with strong internet and air conditioning. Many nomads use it before heading to Posto 9 in the late afternoon.

THE CONTRASTING PLAY — SANTA TERESA LATE AFTERNOON A quieter hilltop alternative If port-zone crowds are not your mood, take the tram over the Arcos from Carioca to Santa Teresa in early afternoon. The yellow tram runs daily from 8am and costs R$20 return. Wander Rua Almirante Alexandrino for artisan shops and the Ruins Park at no charge. Stop at Bar do Mineiro for a pastel and a cold beer around R$25 total. It is quieter than Centro and has that old-Rio feel.

TONIGHT, AFTER 7 PM Low-key dinner and a film For a relaxed evening, book a table at Camarada Camarão in Botafogo for shrimp and cold beer — mains around R$70 to R$100. It stays busy but not chaotic on a Tuesday. In Ipanema, Venga Rooftop serves Spanish tapas and has a terrace open late; count on R$80 to R$120 per person with drinks. Sunset near Arpoador happens around 5:49pm, so arrive just after 6pm to miss the crowd. No major concert is scheduled tonight, so cinema is a safe bet. Estação Net Ipanema often runs Brazilian and independent films with subtitles on some days — check the door screen before buying.

ALSO ON TODAY Museu Nacional de Belas Artes — Centro — open Tue–Sat 11am–5pm, free partial reopening Real Gabinete Português de Leitura — Centro — Mon–Fri 10am–5pm, free Paço Imperial — Praça XV, Centro — Tue–Sun 12pm–6pm, free Parque Lage — Jardim Botânico — 8am–5pm daily, free Feira de São Cristóvão — São Cristóvão — Tue–Thu 10am–6pm, R$10

04

Getting Around

TRANSPORT

The Metrô lines 1, 2 and 4 run normally today. A single journey costs R$8.20 — keep a contactless card or small cash ready. The VLT in the port zone connects Carioca to Praça Mauá for the museums.

If light rain hits after 3pm, expect short surge pricing on ride apps. The seafront ciclovia is open, but ride before 4pm to avoid the shower window.

05

Where to Eat

LUNCH & DINNER

Dinner: Camarada Camarão in Botafogo for shrimp mains R$70–100, or Venga Rooftop in Ipanema for tapas and drinks R$80–120. Book the rooftop ahead if you want a sea view.

06

Practical Info

GOOD TO KNOW

Carry a light rain layer and a fully charged phone for ride apps. Cards and Pix work widely, but keep R$60 in cash for small bars and market snacks.

Museums are free or low-cost today, so bring ID for resident discounts. Avoid the area under the Perimetral around Praça Mauá after dark — stick to the lit museum front and VLT stops.

The sun is strong before clouds build, so use sunscreen even in part-shade mornings.

07

Community & Lifestyle

FOR NEWCOMERS

Most expat meetups are quiet on Tuesday. Try the digital-nomad coffee hour at Co.W. Ipanema around 10am — staff can point you to weekend events.

For Portuguese practice at no cost, a few of the museums today run bilingual captions. Ask at MAR reception; some afternoons they share printed guides in English.

08

Game Day

THE WEEK AHEAD

No Flamengo, Fluminense, Vasco or Botafogo match is scheduled today. The Brasileirão is paused for the FIFA international window and resumes on 7–8 October.

For live football in a bar, The Clover in Praça Seca or Botafogo Praia Shopping’s sports grill usually show midweek league games if any kick off tonight.

Nothing requires a committed watch party today — this is a rest day in the football calendar.

09

Business & Markets

WEEK IN FIGURES

US equity markets carried a risk-on tone into Tuesday, with tech the clear leader. The main story was the pullback in Treasury yields, which eased pressure on growth shares and lifted sentiment broadly.

For Brazil-facing expats the mood is less about local macro and more about global yield direction. A softer 10-year yield and stable volatility suggest investors are comfortable holding risk into the end of the month.

The next watch point is whether US yields stay below the 5% line, as that sets the tone for emerging-market FX and local equity flows this week.

10

Plan Ahead

THE WEEK

THE DAYS AHEAD WED 23 — Partly cloudy, 30% rain — good last dry day for Aterro walk or Santa Teresa tram THU 24 — Rain risk rises to 40% — move museum visits earlier in the day FRI 25 — 55% rain — keep to indoor cafés and coworking SAT 26 — 60% rain — check weekend fixture list before leaving home SUN 27 — Unsettled outlook — Feira de São Cristóvão if cloud clears

11

FAQ

QUICK ANSWERS

Is the port zone safe for a solo visitor on a Tuesday morning?

Yes, around Praça Mauá and the museum fronts it is safe and patrolled from 10am onward. Use the VLT and stay on the main pedestrian routes. After dark, stick to lit tram stops and avoid the old Perimetral underpass.

Which museums are actually open today in Rio?

Museu do Amanhã (10am–6pm, R$30 or R$15 half), MAR (11am–6pm, free Tuesdays), and Museu Nacional de Belas Artes (11am–5pm, free). CCBB is closed on Tuesdays (open Wednesday to Monday) — do not head there today.

Do I need cash or is Pix enough for a day out?

Pix and cards work at most museums and restaurants named here. Keep R$60 in cash for street vendors, the Santa Teresa tram, or small pastel counters. The Metrô single fare is R$8.20 and accepts contactless payment.

World.title: Kenya Work Permit Guide for Foreigners: Fees, Investor Rules and Entry
World.content:
Kenya · Living and Working

Key Facts — What you need Foreigners who want to work, invest or retire in Kenya need a permit or pass from the Directorate of Immigration Services.

— What it costs An employment permit costs 500,000 Kenyan shillings (about US$3,860) a year, plus a 20,000-shilling processing fee (about US$154).

— For investors The Class G investor permit requires proof of at least US$100,000 in capital to be invested in Kenya.

— For remote workers A Class N digital nomad permit costs US$1,000 a year plus a US$200 processing fee.

— For visitors Most tourists need an electronic travel authorisation, which costs US$30 for a single entry.

— The catch A rule requiring visitors to hold at least US$50,000 of health cover is suspended by the High Court, not withdrawn.

Kenya lets many visitors in easily, but living or working there needs a permit with an annual fee. Here is what each route costs and demands.

A buffalo grazes on grassland with the Nairobi skyline behind it. File photograph. (Photo: Timothy A. Gonsalves, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

One-stop reference Company Intelligence Every listed company in Latin America — financials, ownership and structure for 1,450+ companies across 26 exchanges, in one place. Browse the directory →

RT Ask Rio Times Latin American markets, currencies and companies. Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times → RT Ask Rio TimesMarkets, currencies and the economy › RT Ask Rio Times Latin American markets, currencies and companies. × Markets today The currency Rates & inflation Economy outlook Tap a question, or type your own — the answer appears right here. Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

A Kenya work permit is the document that separates a visitor from a resident. Tourists can enter with little paperwork, but anyone who wants to work, invest or retire there needs a permit.

Permits are issued by the Directorate of Immigration Services, part of the Interior Ministry. Applications are filed online through its Foreign Nationals Services portal, known as eFNS.

Fees below are converted at a rate of 129.49 Kenyan shillings to the US dollar. That is the Central Bank of Kenya’s daily rate posted on 21 September 2026.

Getting in: the electronic travel authorisation

Most visitors need an electronic travel authorisation, or eTA, approved before they fly. Kenya introduced the online system in 2024 in place of its old visa regime.

A standard single-entry eTA costs US$30, and a transit eTA costs US$20. A one-year multiple-entry version costs US$300, according to the official eTA website.

Applications are usually processed in three days. The Directorate advises applying at least two weeks before travel, and says an eTA is not a final guarantee of entry.

Many travellers are now exempt under amended rules issued in 2025. The East African Community is a regional bloc of Kenya and its neighbours.

Citizens of six member states may stay up to 180 days without an eTA. They are Burundi, DR Congo, Rwanda, South Sudan, Tanzania and Uganda.

Nationals of a list that includes South Africa, Ghana, Ethiopia, Malaysia and Singapore may stay up to 90 days. Most other African nationals, including Nigerians and Egyptians, get 60 days.

The insurance rule that is on hold

On 30 July 2026, Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale published Gazette Notice No. 11492. It required foreigners staying under 12 months to hold travel health cover of at least US$50,000.

In late August 2026, High Court judge Francis Rayola Olel suspended the rule pending a full hearing. The challenge was brought by two petitioners, while the Consumers Federation of Kenya filed a separate case.

Business Daily, a Nairobi business newspaper, reported on 16 September 2026 that court cases were still stalling the rollout. Travellers should watch for a final ruling.

Working for an employer: Class D

The standard Kenya work permit for employees is Class D. It costs 500,000 Kenyan shillings (about US$3,860) a year, plus a non-refundable processing fee of 20,000 shillings (about US$154).

The employer must show it could not fill the job from the local labour pool. It must also name a Kenyan understudy who will be trained to take over.

Those fees took effect on 1 April 2024 under a government notice of 14 November 2023. The Class D charge rose from 200,000 shillings (about US$1,545), according to advisory firm Vialto Partners.

Traffic at a roundabout in Nairobi, Kenya’s capital. File photograph. (Photo: Matti Blume, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Investors: the Class G permit

Class G covers foreigners who set up a trade, business or consultancy. Applicants must give documentary proof of capital to be invested of at least US$100,000.

The permit costs 250,000 shillings (about US$1,930) a year after the same 20,000-shilling processing fee (about US$154). Applicants also need company registration papers, a shareholder register and a tax compliance certificate.

The Kenya Investment Authority, the state agency that promotes investment and is known as Invest Kenya, helps investors through the process.

Its chief executive, John Mwendwa, told Business Daily in July 2026 that the agency was considering a so-called golden visa. “We are exploring residency by investment,” he said.

No threshold has been set, and he said any scheme would need legislation. A similar plan was first floated in 2019 but never put in place.

Remote workers and retirees

The Class N digital nomad permit was created by amendments to the immigration regulations in 2024. It is for people working remotely for foreign employers or serving clients abroad.

It costs US$1,000 a year plus a US$200 processing fee, and is issued for one or two years. Applicants submit three months of bank statements or payslips.

The official Class N page lists no income minimum. Law firm CMS says the 2024 regulations require an assured income of US$55,000 from sources outside Kenya.

Holders may not work for Kenyan employers, according to the same CMS summary.

Retirees and other financially independent people aged 35 or over can seek a Class K permit. They need an assured income of at least US$24,000 a year from abroad or from a pension.

The Directorate lists a Class K fee of 250,000 shillings (about US$1,930) a year. Class K holders may not take any job or earn income without a permit of the relevant class.

Families and East Africans

Spouses and children of permit holders apply for a dependant’s pass costing 10,000 shillings (about US$77). Dependants of Kenyan citizens pay 20,000 shillings (about US$154).

Citizens of East African Community member states pay no permit fees, according to the Directorate. For everyone else, the annual fee is a recurring cost worth budgeting before signing a lease.

More: Africa coverage, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does a Kenya work permit cost?

It depends on the class. An employment permit, Class D, costs 500,000 Kenyan shillings (about US$3,860) a year, and an investor permit, Class G, costs 250,000 shillings (about US$1,930). Both carry a non-refundable processing fee of 20,000 shillings (about US$154). Citizens of East African Community states pay no fee.

How much must I invest for a Kenyan investor permit?

The Class G permit requires documentary proof of capital to be invested of at least US$100,000. Applicants also submit company incorporation papers, a shareholder register and tax compliance certificates. Kenya has no residency-by-investment programme yet, though Invest Kenya said in July 2026 that it was exploring one.

Does Kenya have a digital nomad visa?

Yes. The Class N permit, created in 2024, is for remote workers employed abroad or serving foreign clients. It costs US$1,000 a year plus a US$200 processing fee and is issued for one or two years. Holders may not work for Kenyan employers.

Do I need an eTA to visit Kenya?

Most visitors do, and a single-entry eTA costs US$30. Citizens of six East African Community states, Burundi, DR Congo, Rwanda, South Sudan, Tanzania and Uganda, are exempt under 2025 rules, as are nationals of dozens of African, Caribbean, Pacific and Asian countries. Holders of Kenyan permits and passes are also exempt.

World.title: Dangote Fertiliser IPO Set for 2028 as Africa’s Richest Man Plans a Second Listing
World.content:
Nigeria · Companies

Key Facts — What happened Aliko Dangote said on 20 September 2026 in New York that his fertiliser company will go public in 2028.

— Where he said it At a Qatar Economic Forum event, powered by Bloomberg, held alongside the United Nations General Assembly.

— Why it matters The Dangote fertiliser IPO would follow the refinery share offer, which closes on 13 October 2026.

— The plant today A US$2.5 billion urea complex near Lagos with capacity of about 3 million tonnes a year.

— The catch In June 2025 Dangote said the fertiliser business would list that same year, so the timetable has slipped.

— What comes next A second urea plant in Ethiopia, jointly owned with the Ethiopian state, and a planned expansion to 12 million tonnes.

Aliko Dangote now has a date for floating his urea business. It comes three years later than he once promised, and while his refinery share sale is still open.

Aliko Dangote, Africa’s richest man, at an international conference; file photograph.

The Dangote fertiliser IPO now has a year attached: 2028. Aliko Dangote, Africa’s richest man, gave the date on Sunday 20 September 2026 in New York.

He spoke at a special edition of the Qatar Economic Forum, a business event powered by Bloomberg. It was held alongside the United Nations General Assembly.

Asked whether he would take his urea business public, he replied: “We will IPO it.”

Asked when, he said: “Yes, it will be 2028.”

Dangote is president and chief executive of Dangote Industries, a Lagos-based conglomerate spanning cement, sugar, fertiliser and fuel refining. His fertiliser arm makes urea, the most widely used nitrogen fertiliser for crops.

“The biggest fertiliser company on earth”

He predicted the listed company would become “the biggest fertiliser company on earth.”

According to Nairametrics, a Lagos financial news site, he described the growth plan in blunt numbers. “We are now going from 3 million tons to 12 million tons of urea,” he said.

He added that the group is opening potash and phosphate mines and will make 2.2 million tonnes of diammonium phosphate. Nairametrics reported his claim that the expansion could meet more than 40% of Africa’s fertiliser needs.

He recalled the 2022 scramble after war in Ukraine disrupted supplies. The African Union sent its chairman, Senegal’s then president Macky Sall, to Russia seeking fertiliser.

A plant near Lagos, and a timetable that slipped

The existing business runs a US$2.5 billion urea complex at Ibeju-Lekki, on the coast east of Lagos, BusinessDay reported. Its capacity is about 3 million tonnes a year.

This is not the first date Dangote has given for the listing. At Afreximbank’s annual meetings in Abuja on 27 June 2025, he said the fertiliser company would join the Nigerian Exchange that year.

At the same event he promised to list the refinery in 2026. That pledge is now on course, with the refinery’s share offer open until 13 October.

The fertiliser flotation, by contrast, has moved back three years.

In New York he did not say which exchange the fertiliser company would use. Nor did he give a size or price for the offer.

Nitrogen fertiliser granules in an open sack; file photograph, not taken at a Dangote plant.

The Ethiopia project gets bigger

Part of the planned growth sits in Ethiopia. On 28 August 2025 Dangote signed a shareholders’ agreement for a US$2.5 billion urea complex at Gode, in the country’s Somali region.

His partner is Ethiopian Investment Holdings, the Ethiopian government’s investment arm, which owns 40%. Dangote holds the other 60%, and the partners set a 40-month build period.

The budget has since grown. In May 2026, company and government statements put total planned spending above US$4 billion, CRU’s trade journal BC Insight reported.

The wider scope adds a gas pipeline, a power plant and a blending unit for mixed fertilisers. Gas is the key raw material for making urea.

The refinery offer sets the scene

The fertiliser news lands in the middle of Nigeria’s biggest share sale. Dangote Petroleum Refinery is offering 4.1 billion shares at ₦525 each (about US$0.39).

If fully subscribed, the offer would raise about ₦2.15 trillion (about US$1.6 billion). Those conversions use the Central Bank of Nigeria’s central rate of 1,329.30 per US dollar on 21 September 2026.

The Securities and Exchange Commission, Nigeria’s capital-markets regulator, cleared the offer in a letter reported on 4 September 2026. Subscriptions opened on 14 September and close on 13 October 2026.

Demand has been strong, The Guardian Nigeria reported, with online platforms straining on opening day. Dangote has called it the “people’s IPO” because of the retail investors taking part.

What the founder wants from the listings

Dangote already controls companies listed in Lagos, including Dangote Cement and Dangote Sugar. His refinery and fertiliser ventures, however, were built as private businesses.

For the refinery offer, he told the New York audience he was seeking 10 million shareholders, ThisDay reported. “We don’t have partners,” he said of those ventures, according to Legit.ng.

“That’s why we are now looking for all these massive number of people to now become our partners,” he added.

In New York he also floated a later New York Stock Exchange listing for the refinery, once its expansion is done. Daily Trust reported that he wants capacity doubled to 1.4 million barrels a day by early 2029.

The same newspaper said he plans more than US$10 billion of investment in power generation. None of these plans has a published prospectus yet.

The practical point for investors is timing. The Dangote fertiliser IPO would open another of his big industrial ventures to outside shareholders, but not before 2028.

More: Africa coverage, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the Dangote fertiliser IPO planned?

Aliko Dangote said it will be in 2028. He gave the date in an on-stage interview at the Qatar Economic Forum’s New York event on Sunday 20 September 2026. He did not name an exchange, an offer size or a price.

Had Dangote promised a fertiliser listing before?

Yes. At the Afreximbank annual meetings in Abuja on 27 June 2025, he said the fertiliser business would list on the Nigerian Exchange in 2025. That did not happen, and the new target is three years later.

How big is the fertiliser business?

Its Lagos-area complex cost about US$2.5 billion and can make about 3 million tonnes of urea a year. Dangote says he wants 12 million tonnes, helped by a jointly owned plant under development at Gode in Ethiopia.

Is the refinery share sale still open?

Yes. The Dangote Petroleum Refinery offer opened on 14 September 2026 and closes on 13 October 2026. It offers 4.1 billion shares at ₦525 each (about US$0.39), worth about ₦2.15 trillion (about US$1.6 billion) if fully taken up.

01 The session in one read

Colombia’s main stock-market index, the COLCAP, closed Monday’s session at 2,566 points, a gain of 0.68% from the previous close. The advance extended a run that has lifted the Bogotá-listed benchmark roughly 37% over the past year.

The Colombian peso moved the other way. One US dollar now buys 3,176 pesos, up 0.30% on the day, meaning the local currency weakened slightly.

The day’s action was driven more by global mood than by a single Colombian story. US stocks rallied, with the Nasdaq up more than 2%, and that appetite for risk spilled into emerging markets including Colombia.

Oil, the commodity most closely tied to Colombia’s exports and state finances, fell about 3%, extending recent declines in crude prices.

Assessment — Global tailwind supports local trend MEDIUM The COLCAP’s gain aligns with the positive tone in US and European equities, which helped lift risk assets broadly. However, the peso’s slight decline suggests currency traders were less enthusiastic, possibly mindful of oil-price fragility and recent record import figures that widened Colombia’s trade deficit. The key variable to watch is whether oil prices can hold current levels. A sustained drop in crude would pressure both the peso and energy-heavy index segments, while any recovery could reinforce the bullish equity case.

02 The day’s numbers

The peso’s 0.30% dip is minor, but it tells a story. With the dollar index up 0.21% against a basket of currencies, the Colombian unit gave back a little ground without any panic.

World.title: Nigeria Viper Helicopters Enter Production as Air Chief Visits Texas Plant
World.content:
Nigeria · Defense

Key Facts — What happened Bell marked the start of production of the Nigeria Viper helicopters in Amarillo, Texas, on 16 September 2026.

— Who was there Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, Nigeria’s Chief of the Air Staff, led the delegation and signed the aircraft’s frame.

— How big the order is Twelve helicopters under a US$455 million production contract awarded by the US Navy in March 2024.

— The wider package Washington approved a sale estimated at US$997 million in April 2022, covering engines, weapons, training and support.

— The catch Bell now projects production will finish in early 2029; the 2024 contract notice expected the work completed in July 2028.

— Why it matters Nigeria’s air force says the Vipers will strengthen operations against jihadist insurgents and other armed groups.

Nigeria’s air force chief watched the first of 12 American attack helicopters take shape in Amarillo. The aircraft are meant for the fight against jihadists and armed gangs.

File photograph of two Brazilian Air Force Black Hawk helicopters in flight. They are not AH-1Z Vipers. (Photo: Rio Times media library)

The first of the Nigeria Viper helicopters is now on the assembly line. Bell, the Texas helicopter maker owned by Textron, marked the start of production at its Amarillo plant on Wednesday 16 September 2026.

The AH-1Z Viper is a twin-engine attack helicopter flown by the US Marine Corps. Nigeria has ordered 12 of them to hunt jihadist fighters and armed gangs from the air.

Nigeria’s air force chief flew in for the occasion. Visiting officials signed the frame of the first aircraft, in what the air force called a beam signing ceremony.

A signature on the first airframe

Air Marshal Sunday Kelvin Aneke, the Chief of the Air Staff, led the Nigerian Air Force delegation. The group toured the production line, according to an air force statement issued on Monday 21 September 2026.

Aneke was appointed by President Bola Tinubu on 24 October 2025, in a reshuffle of all the service chiefs. He was then an Air Vice Marshal.

Aneke called the purchase “an important milestone” in building “a more capable, professional and mission-ready Nigerian Air Force”. The statement was signed by Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, the air force’s director of public relations.

Scott Sims, who runs the H-1 helicopter programme at Bell, described the signed beam in the company’s press release. It would “forever carry the names, hopes, and commitment of those who brought this aircraft to life,” he said.

From approval in 2022 to a contract in 2024

The deal has been four years in the making. On 14 April 2022, the Defense Security Cooperation Agency notified Congress that the State Department had approved a possible sale.

That agency runs Washington’s government-to-government arms sales. Its notice estimated the total programme cost at US$997 million.

The approved package listed 12 helicopters and 28 General Electric T700 engines, four of them spares. It also included 2,000 laser-guidance kits for rockets, 20mm guns, night-vision gear, training and support.

The contract came almost two years later. On 12 March 2024, the US Navy’s aircraft buying command awarded Bell US$455 million for the 12 aircraft.

That contract also covers engineering, programme management and logistics support. The US$997 million estimate covers the whole programme, including engines, weapons, training and support.

The sale runs through Foreign Military Sales, the system in which the Pentagon buys equipment on behalf of allied governments. Nigeria pays, and the US military manages the contracts.

File photograph: Nigerian Army soldiers at a live-fire exercise during Flintlock 20 in Thiès, Senegal, on 17 February 2020. (U.S. Navy photo by Mass Communication Specialist 2nd Class Sean Castellano)

A later finish than first announced

The March 2024 contract notice said the work was expected to be completed in July 2028. Bell now projects production will be completed in early 2029.

No date for the first handover in Nigeria has been reported. Personnel training and in-country maintenance support form part of the package approved in 2022.

Nigeria is the Viper’s third foreign customer, Seapower noted when the contract was signed. Bahrain bought 12, and the Czech Republic is taking new and former Marine Corps aircraft.

Bell has built 189 AH-1Zs for the US Marine Corps, according to Seapower. The type carries a 20mm cannon, rockets and missiles.

What the air force wants them for

Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country, faces several conflicts at once. Jihadist groups fight in the northeast, while armed kidnapping gangs, locally called bandits, terrorise villages in the northwest.

The Viper will strengthen “our counterterrorism and counterinsurgency operations,” Ejodame said in the Bell release. He said the air force looked forward to its induction as “a key platform in our attack helicopter fleet”.

Attack helicopters can loiter over a battlefield and strike small groups with guided weapons. The laser-guidance kits in the package turn ordinary 70mm rockets into precision weapons.

A delicate moment for Washington and Abuja

The ceremony comes after a tense year in relations between the United States and Nigeria. In late 2025, Washington redesignated Nigeria a “country of particular concern” over religious freedom.

That followed threats of military action from President Donald Trump over alleged attacks on Christians. Tinubu rejected the claims, ABC News reported.

He said the characterisation of Nigeria as religiously intolerant “does not reflect our national reality”.

Weeks later, the two governments cooperated. On 25 December 2025, US forces struck Islamic State-linked militants in Sokoto State, in Nigeria’s northwest.

Foreign Minister Yusuf Tuggar said Nigeria had supplied the intelligence and that Tinubu had approved the operation. The Abuja newspaper Premium Times reported his remarks.

The Viper order predates those events. The air force describes the programme as part of a Nigeria–United States defence cooperation programme.

In his statement, Aneke acknowledged the continued cooperation of the United States government.

What comes next

The first of the Nigeria Viper helicopters must now pass through assembly, testing and acceptance in Texas. Bell’s own schedule points to the last of the 12 leaving the line in early 2029.

Aneke stressed the importance of translating the new capabilities into enhanced operational effectiveness, the statement said.

Frequently Asked Questions

What are the Nigeria Viper helicopters?

They are 12 Bell AH-1Z Viper attack helicopters, a twin-engine type flown by the US Marine Corps. Nigeria is buying them through the US Foreign Military Sales system. Production of the first aircraft began at Bell’s plant in Amarillo, Texas, marked by a ceremony on 16 September 2026.

How much is Nigeria paying?

The US Navy awarded Bell a US$455 million contract in March 2024 to build and deliver the 12 aircraft with engineering and logistics support. The State Department approved a sale in April 2022 estimated at US$997 million for the whole programme, including engines, weapons, training and support.

When will Nigeria receive them?

Bell projects production will be completed in early 2029. The March 2024 contract notice said the work was expected to be completed in July 2028. No date for the first handover in Nigeria has been reported.
